229	## Alternatives considered
230	
231	**Best-only promotion.** An earlier design kept one merged head per generation and folded a losing variant back into nothing; every evaluated-but-unpromoted variant is now kept `alive` or `dominated` in a `dsh-archive` ledger, sampled for the next parent in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children) within islands per environment kind — Darwin Gödel Machine archive semantics, where low-scoring ancestors have proven necessary stepping stones toward the eventual best variant. This is rejected as the sole store because best-only hill-climbing has no stepping stones and no transparent lineage to audit for a fabricated result.
232	
233	**Self-selected evaluation cells.** An earlier design let the same proposal choose its own affected cells and predicted deltas before any run, and nothing froze the proposal before results were visible. This is rejected because it lets a semantic stage fund and shape its own evaluation; cells now derive from `SessionDiagnosis` evidence plus component lineage by a logged deterministic rule, and every proposal is content-hashed and frozen before a cell runs.
234	
235	**Reward computed in the implementer's workspace.** An earlier design ran checks against the same tree the implementer had just edited, so a certificate could pass because a test or a fixture was edited rather than because the task was solved. This is rejected because it is directly gameable — editing tests, `conftest.py`, or a package script earns a certificate — and reinforcement learning finds this exploit within tens of steps; checks now run on a pristine fixture plus the implementer's patch under `host` isolation with hidden checks, and a write under check-owned paths is a tamper verdict with reward zero.
236	
237	**Fleet sessions as reinforcement-learning data.** An earlier design for the model pipeline harvested fleet sessions directly for training, but a fleet session carries no environment identity, no group, and no seed, so decontamination, curriculum sampling, and GRPO grouping had nothing to key on. This is rejected in favor of an environment-first, group-first factory: the unit of data is a group of rollouts of one environment under one policy version produced by the runner on demand, and fleet sessions instead feed a short SFT cold start and the environment factory.
238	
239	**A single mutable knowledge store.** An earlier design called distilled skills, presets, and compositions "versioned plugins" but specified no digest, lineage, or generation identity for any of them, so a refined skill overwrote its prior body in place — a single mutable store under a plugin label, with no earlier generation to revert to and no way for a leaderboard to distinguish generations. This is rejected because lineage, decontamination, and rollback all need a stable identity per generation; every component and skill now carries a content-addressed id (`id@digest`) recorded in a log-only `CompositionManifest` event, and the `dsh-archive` ledger keeps every generation, retired ones included.
240	
241	**Judges as gates.** An earlier design let a council's verdict decide blocking outcomes directly in places without excluding judge transcripts from training by default, so a judge whose own prior verdicts could later train the model it judges would acquire a stake in its own future scoring. This is rejected because a same-lineage judge grading an outcome that affects it mislabels far more often than a disinterested one; judge sessions now carry a route distinct from the worker and validator lineage, every judge verdict is advisory until a D gate or a human decides, and judge transcripts default to exclusion from every training export.
242	
243	**Kept open: the artefact-lineage graph view.** An alternative representation draws nodes as durable records (a spec, a completion-standard revision, a certificate, a trajectory line, a dataset manifest, a model release) and edges as the sessions that produced one from another, with agents as edge labels rather than nodes; it makes "follow one artefact" and "diff two runs" native and turns W3 and W4's volumes into a Sankey diagram. It is not adopted here because it needs artefact ids the current schemas do not all carry yet (`SpecDraft`, `Plan`, and `SessionDiagnosis` have no stable identity of their own); it stays a candidate view once those ids exist.
244	
245	**Kept open: training on validator and judge role sessions.** Training the model on the roles its own pipeline needs — validator sessions that authored a standard matching the curated reference, diagnostician sessions, disinterested judge sessions — would let the model improve at those roles the way a verifier-first pipeline trains on its own generator and checker calls. It is not adopted here because judge transcripts default to exclusion from training so a judge never acquires a stake in its own verdicts; whether validator and diagnostician sessions specifically are safe to include is left to be decided per component lineage rather than fixed by this note.
246	
247	## Acceptance criteria
248	
249	### W1
250	
251	- The `environment/run` stamp and a `verification/run` event exist for every executed check, passing or failing, and a keyless test proves a certificate whose cited run is absent, has a different standard revision, or contains a failing check is rejected.
252	- `dsh-archive` records every evaluated `HarnessVariant` as `alive`, `dominated`, or `promoted`, never deletes a dominated entry, and a parent sampler draws from it in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children).
253	- A proposal from the quarantined Harness Engineer that touches an evaluator-owned path (`packages/improvement/**`, `packages/verification/**`, `scripts/run-gates.ts`, or a snapshot fixture) is a hard reject before any cell runs, proven by a fixture that submits such a patch.
254	- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet` (`ctx.fleet`) runs a plan of environment × model × repetition cells through `ctx.environmentRuns` in a fresh workspace per cell, keeps a cell that cannot boot as `{ cell, error }` — a row with an error code, never a missing row — and folds a `LeaderboardRow` per model route and environment that never averages across `isolation` or `heldOut`; both stay columns a consumer partitions by. Its unit spec and its Loader-booted e2e (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/fleet-run`) already cover this.
255	- A model-visible text change produced by the loop — a mutated prompt section, tool schema, or skill body — cannot reach promotion without a human diff review of the re-recorded snapshot expectations.
256	
257	### W2
258	
259	- A keyless snapshot proves the read barrier: an implementer-role tool read under the standard's root is denied by fs policy while the same call from the validator succeeds, and a certificate from a session that composed a log-reading tool is rejected by invariant.
260	- `ProgramLedger` events map every goal of a program to its session, workspace, preset, isolation, budget, and status, and a Loader-booted example resumes a program from the ledger after a restart.
261	- A certificate's `treeHash` equals the merged head before a release record is generated; conflict resolution re-runs the checks rather than re-approving the per-goal certificates.
262	- A `signoff/recorded` event names the principal, the artefact hash, and the evidence in view for spec freeze, security or compliance relaxation, review acceptance, release, and training-data release, and none of these five transitions completes without one.
263	- The project's own checks enter training only after an `EnvironmentAdmission` record shows the pre-state failing, the reference passing, and a gaming-agent run failing to certify, plus a logged human split assignment.
264	
265	### W3
266	
267	- The `environment/run` stamp's content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks are what a decontamination check keys on, and a fixture proves two runs of the same environment hash identically while a changed check hashes differently.
268	- A training run is refused if its reward did not originate from a `verification/run` event, and a fixture proves a write under check-owned paths of the pristine-fixture-plus-patch copy yields a tamper verdict with reward zero.
269	- Truncated, aborted, and errored rollouts are masked rather than scored as failures, proven by a fixture trajectory of each kind carrying no penalty in the training record.
270	- `EvalReport` pins the harness variant hash it ran under, and an evaluation on an unpinned variant is rejected as not comparable.
271	- A `ModelLineage` record generates the Article 53 documentation and the accountable officer's `SignoffRecord` before a `ModelRelease` exists.
272	
273	### W4
274	
275	- A `CompositionManifest` event names every component in play as `id@digest` at session start and on every preset, skill, or tool-set change, and an invariant rejects a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest.
276	- A tier-1 skill candidate carries evidence sessions and a declared scope of session, department, or client, or is rejected by schema; the department scoreboard marks a skill deprecated only after paired present-versus-absent runs show a delta at or below zero over the configured number of runs.
277	- An `ExperimentPlan`'s proposal digest is logged before any of its cells run, and cells trace to `SessionDiagnosis` evidence plus a stratified sample by a logged deterministic rule, never to an S-set priority.
278	- The knowledge ledger's `id@digest` entries and the composition manifest's occurrences agree; a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence is flagged as never having been in play.
279	- Persisted artefacts are hash-chained per checkpoint and signed daily manifests reach write-once storage, and a per-client crypto-shredding key exists before any client-scoped erasure request can be honored.

281	## Rollout
282	
283	1. **Landed** — the `environment/run` stamp, the `verification/run` event, and the runner that appends both: every executed run of a standard, passing or failing, is durable with its executor and workspace tree hash, a certificate needs a fully passing run of its revision, trajectories carry the attempt count, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet` (`ctx.fleet`) runs the cells and folds a leaderboard per route and environment. The `EnvironmentStats` fold that W1 stage 2 and W3 stage 2 read is the scorekeeper's pass@k over the stamped batches; keying it by policy version waits for the stamp to carry one.
284	2. **Blocking** — the read barrier as filesystem and process authority. A validator-root fs-policy plugin, monotonic tool guards, implementer presets without a log-reading tool, and an invariant on certificates; until then every certificate measures only what the implementer could read.
285	3. **Blocking** — attributable decisions and pinned data-use terms. `signoff/recorded`, `decidedBy` with an argument digest on approvals, `dataUse/terms` at session creation, shipped redaction rules, and a curator that records rule hits; without them no client auditor can verify a gate and no transcript may become training data.
286	4. **Major** — content-addressed identity: component and skill digests, and the composition manifest event. Lineage, leaderboards per version, quarantine of dynamic packages, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant all key on `id@digest`.
287	5. **Landed** — the scorekeeper as a session projection (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper`): the `sessionFacts` unit beside goal and verification, a scoreboard folded from persisted logs and partitioned by route, environment, isolation, and held-out split, pass@k over the stamped batches, and a JSONL facts export. What remains is the archive ledger — `HarnessVariant` records over storage with parents, operators, evaluations, and status — and the field groups whose producers do not exist yet.
288	6. **Landed** — the budget policy plugin (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy`): token, wall-time, and cost caps from config, folded from the session log on `agent/pre-step`, a `budget/breach` event, and a durable goal block no round driver resumes; the model sees nothing because the step never opens. What remains is wiring per-cell caps from the fleet plan.
289	7. **Major** — the experiment plugin: staged ladder, paired repetitions, bootstrap intervals, cost. Cells derived by rule, plans frozen and logged; the only place spend decisions live.
290	8. **Major** — structured output for top-level presets as a plugin. Attach the structured-output runtime to a preset's agent context; Intake, Program service, and Trajectory Analyst get forced schemas with logged rejection paths.
291	9. **Major** — trainer operator, model registry, model lineage, environment factory, and admission. W3 end to end, including the Article 53 documentation generated from the lineage record.
292	10. **Minor** — the deny-capable monitor on the tool guard. Impact classes deny by default, ask for a bounded class, and log `oversight/deny`; makes deployment and secrets human gates.
293	11. **Minor** — durable orchestration. Deferred: cells are idempotent by header hash × environment × repetition and recover from persisted child sessions; a journaling workflow engine provider arrives with the program ledger.
294	12. **Minor** — a live run viewer fed by session logs and workflow events. The client's `ui-workflow-run` renders run, phase, and member status only today; a model's-eye view at any seq is the view no competitor can prove complete.
295	
296	## Risks
297	
298	- **Oracle capture.** A patch author re-recording its own snapshot expectations turns a deterministic gate into a rubber stamp; only a human diff review of the recording route defends against it, and it is not automatic anywhere in these workflows.
299	- **Cheap reward under weak isolation.** Under `isolation: none`, checks run with the implementer's privileges in the implementer's own workspace, so a certificate there is not evidence a client or a trainer should treat as strong; leaderboards and training exports must partition by isolation, never blend it.
300	- **Survivorship in the fold.** A session that is skipped, torn by a restart, or interrupted mid-fan-out must still leave a scoreboard row carrying an error code; silently dropping it inflates every certificate rate computed from the remaining rows.
301	- **Data protection before export.** Redaction, consent, and residency events must exist and be enforced before any client transcript reaches an export; an export that runs ahead of the curator plugin and the pinned data-use terms is a confidentiality and residency incident, not a near-miss.
302	- **Judge and reviewer stake.** A judge or reviewer whose own verdicts could later train the model it grades, or whose approval volume is high enough to induce fatigue, degrades toward rubber-stamping; judge transcripts default to exclusion from training, and every human gate stays a named, attributed decision rather than an anonymous one.
303	- **Harness and model co-evolution.** Evaluating a model checkpoint on a harness that evolved against that same checkpoint's predecessor measures the pair, not either alone; `EvalReport` pins the harness variant hash for exactly this reason.
304	- **Orchestration loss.** Hours-long fan-outs run in-process today with no durable resume; without idempotent cells keyed by header hash × environment × repetition, a restart during a long fleet run or a long program double-counts or silently drops work.
305	- **Cost.** Role separation and staged evaluation spend more than a self-judging pipeline; per-goal and per-cell budgets from config, not code constants, are what keeps that cost bounded and visible.

7	## Problem
8	
9	Model-callable surfaces are per-kind and disjoint. Tools are called through `ctx.tools`, skills through the `skill` tool over `ctx.skills`, agents through the `subagent` tool over `ctx.subagents`, workflows through the `workflow` and `ralph` tools, and MCP servers through `dsh-mcp-client` mounting their tools; context providers, presets, bundles, and knowledge sources have no callable identity at all. No registry enumerates what a composition can do, and no identity spans kinds.
10	
11	Nothing attaches to a plugin across its life. Lineage (which plugin a synthesized plugin derived from), provenance (curated versus synthesized), and evidence (which certificates a session earned while the plugin was in play) have no home, so the per-agent scores the [verification seam](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) folds cannot extend to the plugins those agents used.
12	
13	Runtime self-improvement stops at the session edge. [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets an agent define and run a plugin in process memory, and its dynamic packages cannot be promoted automatically by design; a synthesized plugin has no route into a shared catalog, so the loop the Hermes Agent runs for skills (write after use, refine in use, curate the core) and the archive the Darwin Gödel Machine keeps for harness rewrites have no substrate here.
14	
15	A fleet of agents is compositions of compositions: a department is a preset composition of agents, and an agent is a composition of tools, skills, and context plugins. Without one addressing scheme across those levels, leaderboards, judge councils, and promotion policies cannot name what they score.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	Add a component registry [capability seam](../../implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md). A component is one addressable unit of a composition: a plugin, or a plugin-provided member such as a tool, skill, subagent provider, workflow, MCP server, context provider, preset, or composition. The registry records identity, kind, provenance, lineage, membership, and how a model reaches the component; it executes nothing.
20	
21	**Service Definition (`dsh-components`, `ctx.components`).** `ComponentDescriptor` carries a branded `ComponentId`, a `kind` drawn from the merge-extensible `ComponentKindMap` (each producer package declares its kind by declaration merging, so the registry ships no kind of its own), `name`, `description`, the owning package, `provenance` (`curated` or `synthesized`), an optional `lineage` parent id, optional `members` (child component ids, which makes a composition a component), an optional `invoke` pointer (`{ tool, arguments }`: the existing tool a model calls with fixed arguments to reach the component), and kind-specific `detail`. `register()` returns its disposer and rejects a duplicate id loudly; `list(kind?)` and `get(id)` read. Registrations are composition-time effects, not durable session facts.
22	
23	**Producers: one adapter package per seam.** Each adapter mirrors its seam's live registry into components and stays in sync through that seam's own events. `dsh-components-subagents` registers every provider from [`ctx.subagents`](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) as an `agent-provider` component, following `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. The component carries no `invoke` pointer: the `subagent` tool is mounted per provider under a configurable name and takes no `provider` argument, and the subagent seam does not expose which tool instance is bound to a provider; the route appears when the tools adapter mirrors tool-subagent instances with their provider binding. Later adapters do the same for tools, skills, workflows, MCP servers, LLM providers, context providers, and presets. A preset composition registers as a `composition` component whose `members` are the components it mounts; that is the recursion a fleet needs: department, agent preset, then tools, skills, and context.
24	
25	**Consumers.** `/components` (`dsh-command-components`) renders the inventory grouped by kind with provenance and lineage for humans. A later `component_invoke` tool dispatches a component's `invoke` pointer so a model reaches any kind through one call beside the native tools, and Code Mode collapses that into one binding. The verification, improvement, and oversight seams take component ids as the subject of certificates, scores, and audits: a certificate records which components were in play, so scores fold per component exactly as they fold per agent.
26	
27	**Promotion.** A synthesized component registers with `provenance: 'synthesized'` and `lineage` pointing at the component it derived from, whether a `tool-cordis` dynamic package or an agent-authored skill, and is usable in its own session immediately. It enters a shared catalog only through the improvement seam's promotion: sessions where it was in play produced verification certificates, the environment registry's evaluation passes, and a user approves; the promotion record keeps the lineage so later synthesis may branch from any ancestor rather than only the current best. Nothing in this seam promotes automatically.
28	
29	## Recursion at fleet scale
30	
31	An organisation is a composition of departments; a department is a `composition` component whose members are agent-preset components; an agent preset is a `composition` whose members are tool, skill, context, and model-provider components; every member is a plugin. The same descriptor describes every level, and `invoke` on a composition starts a subagent from that preset. Leaderboards fold certificates per component id at every level, so a department, an agent, a skill, and a tool are scored by the same rule, and judge councils address their subjects by the same ids.
32	
33	## Alternatives considered
34	
35	**Make `ctx.tools` the universal registry.** Tool definitions are model-facing schema surface with scoped visibility layers; components include non-callable kinds and need lineage and provenance. A tool is one kind of component and stays where it is.
36	
37	**Use MCP as the universal bus.** MCP is a process and wire protocol outside the harness authority model; tools reached through it lose in-process approval, sandbox policy, and the logged-request invariant unless re-wrapped. MCP servers are one kind, not the bus.
38	
39	**Per-kind lineage and provenance fields inside each seam.** Five copies of the same fields diverge, and no cross-kind identity exists for scoring and councils.
40	
41	**Promote dynamic packages automatically once their tests pass.** The Darwin Gödel Machine incidents and Anthropic's cheating taxonomy show self-authored tests are gameable; promotion needs certificates, held-out evaluation, and approval.
42	
43	**A knowledge-graph database as the registry.** The registry is composition-time truth mirrored from live seams; durable facts (promotion records, certificates) ride session events and the storage domain rather than a new database.
44	
45	**Register components by hand from every producing package.** Mirroring a seam's own registry through an adapter keeps components in sync with that seam's events and adds no obligation to seams that predate the registry.
46	
47	## Acceptance criteria
48	
49	- `dsh-components` ships the Service Definition and in-process registry; a keyless test proves duplicate ids are rejected and that disposing a registration removes the component.
50	- `dsh-components-subagents` mirrors every provider present at mount and every later `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed` edge, and disposing the adapter removes its components.
51	- `/components` renders the grouped inventory through the command registry and writes no session events.
52	- A composition component lists its members, and `component_invoke` on it starts a subagent from that preset in a Loader-booted composition.
53	- A synthesized component with no certificate and no approval is refused entry to the shared catalog by a test that exercises the promotion path.
54	- Every phase lands keyless snapshot scenarios through runnable examples per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
55	
56	## Rollout
57	
58	1. Registry seam, the subagent-provider adapter, and the `/components` command.
59	2. Adapters for tools, skills, workflows, MCP servers, LLM providers, context providers, and presets; the `composition` kind; the `component_invoke` tool.
60	3. Promotion: synthesized provenance from `tool-cordis` and skill authoring, certificates as component evidence, improvement-seam evaluation, approval, and the lineage archive.
61	
62	## Risks
63	
64	Mirror drift: an adapter that misses a seam event shows a component that no longer exists. Adapters bind to the seam's own events and register through effects, and disposal tests cover both edges.
65	
66	Two callable surfaces: `component_invoke` beside native tools may split model attention. Native tools remain primary; the uniform call serves kinds without a tool of their own, as Code Mode already collapses many schemas into one binding.
67	
68	Identity stability: ids derive from the kind and the seam's own stable name, never from mount order, so a remount produces the same id.
69	
70	Promotion gaming: identical resubmission, format mimicry, and disguised intent apply to plugins as they do to tasks; the promotion path reuses the verification seam's isolation and the oversight seam's cross-lineage judges.
71

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the component domain: identities, the merge-extensible kind
3	 * map, descriptors, and the invoke pointer, free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
9	
10	/** Identifies one component; derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order. */
11	export type ComponentId = Branded<'ComponentId'>
12	
13	/**
14	 * Merge-extensible map from component kind to that kind's detail type. Each
15	 * producer package declares its kind by declaration merging; the registry
16	 * itself ships no kind.
17	 */
18	export interface ComponentKindMap {}
19	
20	/** Every declared component kind; `string` while no producer has merged a kind into the program. */
21	export type ComponentKind = [keyof ComponentKindMap] extends [never] ? string : Extract<keyof ComponentKindMap, string>
22	
23	/** Kind-specific detail declared by the kind's producer; `unknown` for kinds outside this program. */
24	export type ComponentDetail<K extends string> = K extends keyof ComponentKindMap ? ComponentKindMap[K] : unknown
25	
26	/** Whether people curated a component or an agent synthesized it. */
27	export type ComponentProvenance = 'curated' | 'synthesized'
28	
29	/** The existing tool a model calls, with fixed arguments, to reach a component. */
30	export interface ComponentInvoke {
31	  /** Registered tool name. */
32	  readonly tool: string
33	  /** Arguments fixed by the component; the model supplies the rest. */
34	  readonly arguments?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
35	}
36	
37	/** One addressable unit of a composition. */
38	export interface ComponentDescriptor<K extends ComponentKind = ComponentKind> {
39	  /** Stable identity across compositions. */
40	  readonly id: ComponentId
41	  /** Declared kind. */
42	  readonly kind: K
43	  /** Human-readable name. */
44	  readonly name: string
45	  /** What the component does, stated for people and models. */
46	  readonly description: string
47	  /** Package that produced the registration. */
48	  readonly owner: string
49	  /** Curated by people or synthesized by an agent. */
50	  readonly provenance: ComponentProvenance
51	  /** Component this one derived from, absent for roots. */
52	  readonly lineage?: ComponentId
53	  /** Child components of a composition, absent for leaves. */
54	  readonly members?: readonly ComponentId[]
55	  /** How a model reaches the component, absent for kinds without a callable route. */
56	  readonly invoke?: ComponentInvoke
57	  /** Kind-specific detail. */
58	  readonly detail: ComponentDetail<K>
59	}

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/**
2	 * Component registry: identity, kind, provenance, lineage, membership, and the
3	 * callable route of every addressable unit in a composition. The registry
4	 * executes nothing and holds composition-time state only. The
5	 * [component-registry Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md)
6	 * owns the design rationale.
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components
8	 */
9	
10	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
11	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { ComponentDescriptor, ComponentId as ComponentIdType, ComponentKind } from './types.ts'
13	
14	export type * from './types.ts'
15	
16	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
17	  interface Context {
18	    components: ComponentRegistry
19	  }
20	}
21	
22	/** Stable error codes for rejected component registrations. */
23	export type ComponentErrorCode = 'COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID'
24	
25	/** Error returned by the component registry boundary. */
26	export class ComponentError extends HarnessError {
27	  /**
28	   * @param message - human-readable rejection reason.
29	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
30	   */
31	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
32	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
33	  constructor(message: string, code: ComponentErrorCode) {
34	    super(message, code)
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * Brand a string as a component id.
40	 * @param id - raw component identifier.
41	 * @returns the same string with the compile-time brand.
42	 */
43	export function ComponentId(id: string): ComponentIdType {
44	  return id as ComponentIdType
45	}
46	
47	/** Copy a descriptor so callers never share the registry's stored arrays. */
48	function detach(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): ComponentDescriptor {
49	  return {
50	    ...descriptor,
51	    ...descriptor.members === undefined ? {} : { members: [...descriptor.members] },
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/** Component registry (`ctx.components`): the composition-time inventory mirrored from live seams. */
56	export class ComponentRegistry extends Service {
57	  private readonly components = new Map<ComponentIdType, ComponentDescriptor>()
58	
59	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
60	    super(ctx, 'components')
61	  }
62	
63	  /**
64	   * Register one component. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps the
65	   * returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the component.
66	   * @param descriptor - complete component description.
67	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
68	   * @throws {@link ComponentError} when the id is already registered.
69	   */
70	  register(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): () => void {
71	    if (this.components.has(descriptor.id)) {
72	      throw new ComponentError(`component "${descriptor.id}" is already registered`, 'COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID')
73	    }
74	    const stored = detach(descriptor)
75	    this.components.set(stored.id, stored)
76	    return () => {
77	      if (this.components.get(stored.id) === stored) this.components.delete(stored.id)
78	    }
79	  }
80	
81	  /**
82	   * Read one component.
83	   * @param id - component identity.
84	   * @returns a detached descriptor, or `undefined` when nothing is registered under the id.
85	   */
86	  get(id: ComponentIdType): ComponentDescriptor | undefined {
87	    const stored = this.components.get(id)
88	    return stored === undefined ? undefined : detach(stored)
89	  }
90	
91	  /**
92	   * List components in registration order.
93	   * @param kind - when given, only components of this kind.
94	   * @returns detached descriptors.
95	   */
96	  list(kind?: ComponentKind): ComponentDescriptor[] {
97	    return [...this.components.values()]
98	      .filter(component => kind === undefined || component.kind === kind)
99	      .map(detach)
100	  }
101	}
102	
103	export default ComponentRegistry

1	/**
2	 * Agent skill provider registry.
3	 *
4	 * This package owns the Service Definition role of the skill capability seam.
5	 * Concrete
6	 * providers such as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` decide where skills come
7	 * from; this service only merges provider catalogs, resolves the winning skill
8	 * for a name, and exposes the winning summaries and definitions to consumers.
9	 *
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill
11	 */
12	
13	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
15	import { NamedEntries, ScopedLayers, scopeChainOf, scopeOf } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
16	import type { ScopeKey, ScopeLayer } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
17	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
18	import type Schema from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
19	
20	const SKILL_NAME = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/
21	const DEFAULT_COLLECT_CACHE_ENTRIES = 128
22	const MAX_COLLECT_ATTEMPTS = 2
23	const RUNTIME_PROVIDER = 'runtime'
24	const RUNTIME_RANK = 250
25	
26	/** Standard precedence rank for packaged skill providers and local bundled roots. */
27	export const BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK = 600
28	
29	/**
30	 * Return whether a string is a valid kebab-case skill name.
31	 * @param name - candidate skill name to validate.
32	 * @returns whether the name matches the public skill-name grammar.
33	 */
34	export function isSkillName(name: string): boolean {
35	  return SKILL_NAME.test(name)
36	}
37	
38	/** Origin bucket for a skill contribution. The value is prompt-visible metadata, not precedence by itself. */
39	export type SkillSource = 'project-dsh' | 'project-agents' | 'runtime' | 'user-dsh' | 'user-agents' | 'custom' | 'bundled' | (string & {})
40	
41	/** Optional provider-specific base used by loaded skill bodies to resolve relative resources. */
42	export type SkillResourceBase =
43	  | { readonly kind: 'directory'; readonly path: string }
44	  | { readonly kind: 'url'; readonly url: string }
45	  | { readonly kind: 'opaque'; readonly description: string }
46	
47	/** Invocation controls shared by skill discovery consumers. */
48	export interface SkillInvocationPolicy {
49	  /** Whether model-facing catalogs and loaders include this skill. */
50	  readonly modelInvocable: boolean
51	  /** Whether human-facing command catalogs and loaders include this skill. */
52	  readonly userInvocable: boolean
53	}
54	
55	/** Invocation-neutral skill metadata returned by `ctx.skills.list()`. */
56	export interface SkillSummary {
57	  /** Kebab-case identifier used to address the skill. */
58	  readonly name: string
59	  /** Short routing description shown by discovery consumers. */
60	  readonly description: string
61	  /** Optional extra routing guidance. */
62	  readonly whenToUse?: string
63	  /** Resolved model and user invocation controls. */
64	  readonly invocation: SkillInvocationPolicy
65	  /** Discovery source that produced this winning skill. */
66	  readonly source: SkillSource
67	  /** Provider that owns this skill body. */
68	  readonly provider: string
69	  /** Provider-specific base for relative resources. */
70	  readonly resourceBase?: SkillResourceBase
71	}
72	
73	/** Provider catalog entry used by the registry to merge and later load skills. */
74	export interface SkillCandidate extends SkillSummary {
75	  /** Lower ranks win duplicate skill names before provider registration order is considered. */
76	  readonly rank: number
77	  /** Opaque provider-owned handle passed back to `provider.get()`. */
78	  readonly locator: unknown
79	  /** Absolute file path when the provider has one. */
80	  readonly path?: string
81	  /** Parsed optional metadata object from provider-specific skill frontmatter. */
82	  readonly metadata?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>
83	}
84	
85	/** Complete parsed skill definition, including the body loaded by `ctx.skills.get()`. */
86	export interface SkillDefinition extends SkillSummary {
87	  /** Markdown instruction body after any provider-specific metadata removal. */
88	  readonly content: string
89	  /** Absolute file path when the skill came from disk. */
90	  readonly path?: string
91	  /** Parsed optional metadata object from frontmatter. */
92	  readonly metadata?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>
93	}
94	
95	/** Runtime skill contribution accepted by `ctx.skills.register()`. */
96	export type SkillRegistration = Omit<SkillDefinition, 'invocation' | 'provider'> & {
97	  /** Invocation controls; omission permits both model and user surfaces. */
98	  readonly invocation?: SkillInvocationPolicy
99	  /** Provider label; omission uses the registry-owned runtime provider. */
100	  readonly provider?: string
101	}
102	
103	/** Caller context used for cwd-sensitive and abortable provider work. */
104	export interface SkillLookupOptions {
105	  /** Workspace selector for the current lookup. */
106	  readonly cwd?: string | undefined
107	  /** Abort discovery or loading work for the current caller. */
108	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined
109	}
110	
111	/**
112	 * Registry read options: provider lookup context plus the viewing scope.
113	 * The registry consumes `scope` to select layers; providers receive the same
114	 * borrowed options object and read only their {@link SkillLookupOptions}
115	 * contract from it.
116	 */
117	export interface SkillViewOptions extends SkillLookupOptions {
118	  /** Viewing scope (the calling agent); omitted reads the global layer alone. */
119	  readonly scope?: ScopeKey | undefined
120	}
121	
122	/**
123	 * Return whether a skill may be advertised to and loaded by a model.
124	 * @param skill - skill metadata carrying resolved invocation controls.
125	 * @returns whether the policy permits model invocation.
126	 */
127	export function isModelInvocable(skill: Pick<SkillSummary, 'invocation'>): boolean {
128	  return skill.invocation.modelInvocable
129	}
130	
131	/**
132	 * Return whether a skill may be advertised to and loaded by a human-facing command.
133	 * @param skill - skill metadata carrying resolved invocation controls.
134	 * @returns whether the policy permits user invocation.
135	 */
136	export function isUserInvocable(skill: Pick<SkillSummary, 'invocation'>): boolean {
137	  return skill.invocation.userInvocable
138	}
139	
140	/**
141	 * Durable source for the context message a user-explicit skill invocation
142	 * injects: the user's own words ride a plain user message, and the rendered
143	 * skill body follows as injected `instructions`-form context carrying this
144	 * source, so transcript consumers present the injection from metadata
145	 * instead of re-parsing the model-facing text.
146	 */
147	export interface SkillInvocationSource {
148	  readonly kind: 'skill-invocation'
149	  /** Invoked skill name, validated user-invocable at the injecting boundary. */
150	  readonly name: string
151	  /** Injected skill bodies are instructions for the model to follow. */
152	  readonly form: 'instructions'
153	}
154	
155	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm' {
156	  interface MessageSourceMap {
157	    /** A user-explicit skill invocation injected by the host. */
158	    'skill-invocation': SkillInvocationSource
159	  }
160	}
161	
162	/**
163	 * Render one loaded skill for the model. The output is shared verbatim by the
164	 * `skill` tool result and the user-explicit invocation injection, so the model
165	 * sees one canonical `<skill_content>` shape on both paths. The name rides an
166	 * escaped attribute; the body is embedded verbatim (skills are trusted local
167	 * content, and user-supplied invocation text stays outside this wrapper).
168	 * @param skill - name, provider, optional resource base, and body to render.
169	 * @returns the complete model-facing `<skill_content>` block.
170	 */
171	export function renderSkillContent(skill: Pick<SkillDefinition, 'name' | 'provider' | 'resourceBase' | 'content'>): string {
172	  const resourceHint = renderResourceHint(skill)
173	  return [
174	    `<skill_content name="${escapeAttr(skill.name)}">`,
175	    '<skill_resources>',
176	    ...resourceHint,
177	    '</skill_resources>',
178	    '',
179	    '<skill_instructions>',
180	    skill.content,
181	    '</skill_instructions>',
182	    '</skill_content>',
183	  ].join('\n')
184	}
185	
186	function renderResourceHint(skill: Pick<SkillDefinition, 'provider' | 'resourceBase'>): string[] {
187	  const base = skill.resourceBase
188	  if (base === undefined) {
189	    return [
190	      `Resources for this skill are managed by provider "${escapeText(skill.provider)}".`,
191	      'Load referenced resources only as needed.',
192	    ]
193	  }
194	  switch (base.kind) {
195	    case 'directory':
196	      return [
197	        `Base directory for this skill: ${escapeText(base.path)}`,
198	        'Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.',
199	      ]
200	    case 'url':
201	      return [
202	        `Base URL for this skill: ${escapeText(base.url)}`,
203	        'Resolve relative URLs mentioned by this skill against the base URL before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.',
204	      ]
205	    case 'opaque':
206	      return [
207	        `Resources for this skill: ${escapeText(base.description)}`,
208	        'Load referenced resources only as needed.',
209	      ]
210	    /* v8 ignore start -- SkillResourceBase is a closed union; a future kind must fail compilation here. */
211	    default:
212	      return assertNever(base, 'SkillResourceBase.kind')
213	    /* v8 ignore stop */
214	  }
215	}
216	
217	function escapeAttr(value: string): string {
218	  return value.replaceAll('&', '&').replaceAll('"', '"').replaceAll('<', '<')
219	}
220	
221	/**
222	 * Escape model-facing prose embedded inside skill markup so provider-supplied
223	 * text cannot open or close framing tags.
224	 * @param value - raw prose to embed.
225	 * @returns the escaped text.
226	 */
227	export function escapeText(value: string): string {
228	  return value.replaceAll('&', '&').replaceAll('<', '<').replaceAll('>', '>')
229	}
230	
231	/** One catalog observation plus whether discovery completed within a stable catalog revision. */
232	export interface SkillCatalogSnapshot {
233	  /** Sorted invocation-neutral summaries collected in this observation. */
234	  readonly skills: SkillSummary[]
235	  /** Whether every registered provider completed without a concurrent catalog revision. */
236	  readonly complete: boolean
237	}
238	
239	/** Provider candidates plus whether the current discovery is authoritative. */
240	export interface SkillProviderObservation {
241	  /** Candidates available from the current provider discovery. */
242	  readonly candidates: readonly SkillCandidate[]
243	  /** Whether discovery completed and these candidates may be cached. */
244	  readonly complete: boolean
245	}
246	
247	/** Provider interface for one source of skills, such as local directories or a remote registry. */
248	export interface SkillProvider {
249	  /** Unique provider name in the `ctx.skills` registry. */
250	  readonly name: string
251	  /**
252	   * List available skill candidates for the current lookup context. Provider
253	   * plugins register synchronously during `apply()`; remote initialization,
254	   * authentication, and discovery are awaited inside this method. Implementations
255	   * should settle promptly when `options.signal` aborts.
256	   * @param options - lookup options; `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills and `signal` cancels work.
257	   * @returns provider candidates as a complete-array shorthand, or an explicit
258	   *   observation when usable candidates came from incomplete discovery.
259	   */
260	  readonly list: (options: SkillLookupOptions) => Promise<readonly SkillCandidate[] | SkillProviderObservation>
261	  /**
262	   * Load a complete skill body for a previously listed candidate.
263	   * @param candidate - the winning candidate originally returned by this provider.
264	   * @param options - lookup options; `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills and `signal` cancels work.
265	   * @returns the full skill body, or `undefined` if it is no longer loadable.
266	   */
267	  readonly get: (candidate: SkillCandidate, options: SkillLookupOptions) => Promise<SkillDefinition | undefined>
268	}
269	
270	/** Registration-scoped lifecycle and invalidation capability borrowed by one provider. */
271	export interface SkillProviderControl {
272	  /** Aborts if registration fails or when the exact provider registration is disposed. */
273	  readonly signal: AbortSignal
274	  /** Invalidate completed catalogs and notify consumers only while the exact registration remains active. */
275	  readonly invalidate: () => void
276	}
277	
278	/** Skill registry configuration. */
279	export interface Config {
280	  /** Maximum number of completed cwd/provider catalogs kept in memory. */
281	  readonly collectCacheMaxEntries?: number
282	}
283	
284	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
285	  interface Context {
286	    skills: SkillRegistry
287	  }
288	
289	  interface Events {
290	    /**
291	     * A skill provider, runtime contribution, or provider-backed catalog may
292	     * have changed. This is an unfiltered invalidation notification; consumers
293	     * refetch the catalog for their own lookup options. Listener failures are
294	     * contained and cannot veto the registry mutation.
295	     * @mode emit
296	     */
297	    'skills/change'(): void
298	  }
299	}
300	
301	interface IndexedCandidate {
302	  candidate: SkillCandidate
303	  provider: SkillProvider
304	  providerOrder: number
305	  localOrder: number
306	  /** Owning layer, so a stale-definition invalidation can verify the exact registration is still live. */
307	  layer: SkillLayer
308	}
309	
310	/** One provider registration retained by its layer. */
311	interface RegisteredProvider {
312	  provider: SkillProvider
313	  /** Service-wide monotonic registration order, the within-layer rank tiebreak. */
314	  order: number
315	}
316	
317	interface LayerCollectResult {
318	  entries: IndexedCandidate[]
319	  cacheable: boolean
320	}
321	
322	interface CollectResult {
323	  entries: Map<string, IndexedCandidate>
324	  cacheable: boolean
325	}
326	
327	/** One scope's complete skill-registry contribution. */
328	class SkillLayer implements ScopeLayer {
329	  /** Providers registered through contexts carrying this scope, insertion-ordered. */
330	  readonly providers: NamedEntries<RegisteredProvider>
331	  /** Runtime skills registered through contexts carrying this scope. */
332	  readonly runtime = new Map<string, SkillDefinition>()
333	
334	  constructor(scope: ScopeKey | undefined) {
335	    this.providers = new NamedEntries(name => new Error(scope === undefined
336	      ? `a skill provider named "${name}" is already registered`
337	      : `a skill provider named "${name}" is already registered in this scope`))
338	  }
339	
340	  /** Whether every contribution table in this aggregate layer is empty. */
341	  isEmpty(): boolean {
342	    return this.providers.isEmpty() && this.runtime.size === 0
343	  }
344	}
345	
346	/**
347	 * Layered registry of skill providers, the host+per-scope shape the tools
348	 * registry established. A registration files into the layer of its calling
349	 * context's scope ({@link scopeOf}): host rows and repository plugins land in
350	 * the global layer, while a plugin mounted by an agent preset's standing
351	 * composition lands in that preset's layer. A read merges the global layer
352	 * with the viewing scope's chain — the nearest layer's entry wins a duplicate
353	 * name outright, and the rank order decides duplicates only within one layer.
354	 * It exposes sorted invocation-neutral summaries and loads full skill bodies
355	 * on demand.
356	 */
357	export class SkillRegistry extends Service {
358	  static Config: Schema<Config> = z.object({
359	    collectCacheMaxEntries: z.number().default(DEFAULT_COLLECT_CACHE_ENTRIES),
360	  })
361	
362	  private readonly collectCacheMaxEntries: number
363	  private readonly layers = new ScopedLayers<SkillLayer>(
364	    scope => new SkillLayer(scope),
365	    () => { this.invalidateCache() },
366	  )
367	  private readonly collectCache = new Map<string, Map<string, IndexedCandidate>>()
368	  private revision = 0
369	  private nextProviderOrder = 0
370	  /** Stable identities for cache keys; scope keys are opaque identity-compared objects. */
371	  private readonly scopeIds = new WeakMap<ScopeKey, number>()
372	  private nextScopeId = 1
373	
374	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
375	    super(ctx, 'skills')
376	    this.collectCacheMaxEntries = config.collectCacheMaxEntries ?? DEFAULT_COLLECT_CACHE_ENTRIES
377	    assertPositiveInteger('collectCacheMaxEntries', this.collectCacheMaxEntries)
378	  }
379	
380	  /**
381	   * Register a borrowed same-process provider synchronously during plugin
382	   * apply, into the calling context's layer: a scoped context (an agent
383	   * preset's standing mount) registers for that scope alone, an unscoped
384	   * context registers globally. Duplicate names within one layer and reserved
385	   * names throw; remote initialization belongs in `list()`. Fiber disposal
386	   * unregisters the provider and invalidates catalog caches.
387	   * @param create - synchronous factory receiving this registration's lifecycle and invalidation control.
388	   * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer that unregisters this provider;
389	   *   composite effects may yield it directly to preserve teardown ordering.
390	   */
391	  registerProvider(create: (control: SkillProviderControl) => SkillProvider): () => void {
392	    const lifecycle = new AbortController()
393	    let registration: { layer: SkillLayer; name: string } | undefined
394	    let provider: SkillProvider
395	    const control: SkillProviderControl = {
396	      signal: lifecycle.signal,
397	      invalidate: () => {
398	        const active = registration
399	        if (active !== undefined && active.layer.providers.get(active.name)?.provider === provider) {
400	          this.invalidateCache()
401	        }
402	      },
403	    }
404	    try {
405	      provider = create(control)
406	      const name = provider.name
407	      if (name === RUNTIME_PROVIDER) {
408	        throw new Error(`"${RUNTIME_PROVIDER}" is reserved for runtime skill registrations`)
409	      }
410	      const order = this.nextProviderOrder
411	      this.nextProviderOrder += 1
412	      return this.layers.effect(
413	        this.ctx,
414	        (layer) => {
415	          const undo = layer.providers.insert(name, { provider, order })
416	          registration = { layer, name }
417	          return () => {
418	            registration = undefined
419	            undo()
420	            lifecycle.abort(new Error(`skill provider "${name}" disposed`))
421	          }
422	        },
423	        { label: 'skills.registerProvider()' },
424	      )
425	    } catch (error) {
426	      lifecycle.abort(error)
427	      throw error
428	    }
429	  }
430	
431	  /**
432	   * Register a borrowed readonly runtime skill into the calling context's
433	   * layer. Project entries outrank runtime entries, which outrank user
434	   * entries, within one layer. Same-name runtime entries in one layer are
435	   * first-wins; a duplicate logs a warning and receives a no-op disposer so
436	   * it cannot remove the winner.
437	   * @param skill - the skill definition input; omitted invocation and provider fields receive defaults.
438	   * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer, preserving composite teardown order and invalidating caches.
439	   */
440	  register(skill: SkillRegistration): () => void {
441	    validateRuntimeSkill(skill)
442	    const scope = scopeOf(this.ctx)
443	    const existingLayer = scope === undefined ? this.layers.global : this.layers.peek(scope)
444	    if (existingLayer !== undefined && existingLayer.runtime.has(skill.name)) {
445	      this.ctx.logger.warn(`runtime skill "${skill.name}" ignored because it is already registered`)
446	      return () => {}
447	    }
448	    const definition: SkillDefinition = {
449	      ...skill,
450	      invocation: skill.invocation ?? { modelInvocable: true, userInvocable: true },
451	      provider: skill.provider ?? RUNTIME_PROVIDER,
452	    }
453	    return this.layers.effect(
454	      this.ctx,
455	      (layer) => {
456	        layer.runtime.set(definition.name, definition)
457	        return () => { layer.runtime.delete(definition.name) }
458	      },
459	      { label: 'skills.register()' },
460	    )
461	  }
462	
463	  /**
464	   * List invocation-neutral skill summaries for a workspace. Consumers apply
465	   * model or user invocation policy at their operational boundary. Lookup
466	   * options and provider candidates are readonly same-process values borrowed
467	   * throughout discovery.
468	   * @param options - view options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers, `cwd` selects project roots, and `signal` cancels discovery.
469	   * @returns all sorted winning summaries.
470	   */
471	  async list(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillSummary[]> {
472	    return (await this.snapshot(options)).skills
473	  }
474	
475	  /**
476	   * Observe the current invocation-neutral catalog and whether discovery completed within a stable revision.
477	   * Incomplete observations are never cached, allowing consumers to retain last-good state and
478	   * retry on their next request boundary.
479	   * @param options - view options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers, `cwd` selects project roots, and `signal` cancels discovery.
480	   * @returns sorted summaries plus discovery-completeness state.
481	   */
482	  async snapshot(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillCatalogSnapshot> {
483	    const collected = await this.collect(options)
484	    return {
485	      skills: [...collected.entries.values()]
486	        .map(entry => toSummary(entry.candidate))
487	        .sort(compareSkillSummary),
488	      complete: collected.cacheable,
489	    }
490	  }
491	
492	  /**
493	   * Load and validate the winning candidate, passing its opaque discovery locator back to the
494	   * provider. Cancellation is rechecked after selection, including cache hits, and raced against
495	   * loading so an uncooperative provider cannot hang the caller.
496	   * @param name - kebab-case skill name.
497	   * @param options - view options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers,
498	   *   `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills, and `signal` cancels work.
499	   * @returns the full skill, including body content, or `undefined`.
500	   */
501	  async get(name: string, options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillDefinition | undefined> {
502	    if (!isSkillName(name)) return undefined
503	    const collected = await this.collect(options)
504	    throwIfAborted(options.signal)
505	    const match = collected.entries.get(name)
506	    if (match === undefined) return undefined
507	    const definition = await waitWithAbort(
508	      match.provider.get(match.candidate, options),
509	      options.signal,
510	    )
511	    if (definition === undefined) return undefined
512	    validateDefinition(definition)
513	    if (definition.name !== match.candidate.name) {
514	      this.invalidateEntry(match)
515	      return undefined
516	    }
517	    return definition
518	  }
519	
520	  private async collect(options: SkillViewOptions): Promise<CollectResult> {
521	    throwIfAborted(options.signal)
522	    let attempt = 1
523	    while (true) {
524	      const revision = this.revision
525	      // The chain is part of the key rather than assumed stable: a blank-session
526	      // recompose re-parents an existing scope without touching this registry,
527	      // and only a chain-bearing key makes the next read see the new preset.
528	      const key = this.collectCacheKey(options.cwd, scopeChainOf(options.scope), revision)
529	      const cached = this.collectCache.get(key)
530	      if (cached !== undefined) return { entries: cached, cacheable: true }
531	
532	      const result = await this.collectFresh(options)
533	      throwIfAborted(options.signal)
534	      if (revision !== this.revision) {
535	        if (attempt < MAX_COLLECT_ATTEMPTS) {
536	          attempt += 1
537	          continue
538	        }
539	        return { entries: result.entries, cacheable: false }
540	      }
541	      if (result.cacheable) {
542	        this.collectCache.set(key, result.entries)
543	        if (this.collectCache.size > this.collectCacheMaxEntries) {
544	          const oldest = this.collectCache.keys().next() as IteratorYieldResult<string>
545	          this.collectCache.delete(oldest.value)
546	        }
547	      }
548	      return result
549	    }

552	  private async collectFresh(options: SkillViewOptions): Promise<CollectResult> {
553	    // Global first, then existing chain overlays farthest ancestor first and
554	    // the exact scope last, so the nearest layer's same-name entry replaces
555	    // the farther ones — the tools registry's shadowing rule. Rank decides
556	    // duplicates only within one layer.
557	    const layers = [this.layers.global, ...this.layers.chainLayers(options.scope)]
558	    const merged = new Map<string, IndexedCandidate>()
559	    let cacheable = true
560	    for (const layer of layers) {
561	      const collected = await this.collectLayer(layer, options)
562	      if (!collected.cacheable) cacheable = false
563	      for (const entry of collected.entries) merged.set(entry.candidate.name, entry)
564	    }
565	    return { entries: merged, cacheable }
566	  }

568	  private async collectLayer(layer: SkillLayer, options: SkillLookupOptions): Promise<LayerCollectResult> {
569	    const collected = await this.listLayerCandidates(layer, options)
570	    collected.entries.sort(compareIndexedCandidates)
571	    const seen = new Set<string>()
572	    const result: IndexedCandidate[] = []
573	    for (const entry of collected.entries) {
574	      const skill = entry.candidate
575	      if (seen.has(skill.name)) {
576	        this.ctx.logger.warn(`skill "${skill.name}" from ${skill.source} ignored because a higher-priority skill already exists`)
577	        continue
578	      }
579	      seen.add(skill.name)
580	      result.push(entry)
581	    }
582	    return { entries: result, cacheable: collected.cacheable }
583	  }

585	  private async listLayerCandidates(layer: SkillLayer, options: SkillLookupOptions): Promise<LayerCollectResult> {
586	    throwIfAborted(options.signal)
587	    const candidates: IndexedCandidate[] = []
588	    let cacheable = true
589	    let runtimeOrder = 0
590	    for (const skill of [...layer.runtime.values()].sort((a, b) => compareCodePoints(a.name, b.name))) {
591	      candidates.push({
592	        candidate: runtimeCandidate(skill),
593	        provider: RUNTIME_SKILL_PROVIDER,
594	        providerOrder: -1,
595	        localOrder: runtimeOrder,
596	        layer,
597	      })
598	      runtimeOrder += 1
599	    }
600	    for (const { provider, order } of [...layer.providers.values()]) {
601	      let localOrder = 0
602	      let output: unknown
603	      try {
604	        output = await waitWithAbort(provider.list(options), options.signal)
605	      } catch (error) {
606	        if (options.signal?.aborted === true) throw toError(options.signal.reason)
607	        cacheable = false
608	        this.ctx.logger.warn(`skill provider "${provider.name}" skipped: ${errorMessage(error)}`)
609	      }
610	      if (output === undefined) continue
611	      const observation = normalizeProviderObservation(output, provider.name)
612	      if (!observation.complete) cacheable = false
613	      for (const candidate of observation.candidates) {
614	        validateCandidate(candidate, provider.name)
615	        candidates.push({ candidate, provider, providerOrder: order, localOrder, layer })
616	        localOrder += 1
617	      }
618	    }
619	    return { entries: candidates, cacheable }
620	  }

731	  if (typeof candidate.provider !== 'string') {

819	function waitWithAbort<T>(promise: Promise<T>, signal: AbortSignal | undefined): Promise<T> {
820	  if (signal === undefined) return promise
821	  throwIfAborted(signal)
822	  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
823	    const cleanup = (): void => {
824	      signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
825	    }
826	    const onAbort = (): void => {
827	      cleanup()
828	      reject(toError(signal.reason))
829	    }
830	    signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
831	    void promise.then(
832	      (value) => {
833	        cleanup()
834	        resolve(value)
835	      },
836	      (error: unknown) => {
837	        cleanup()
838	        reject(toError(error))
839	      },
840	    )
841	  })
842	}

846	  if (signal?.aborted === true) throw toError(signal.reason)
847	}

851	  try {
852	    if (error instanceof Error) return error
853	  } catch {
854	    // A hostile proxy may throw during instanceof; fall through to the total renderer.
855	  }
856	  return new Error(errorMessage(error))
857	}

297	  async observeRoots(roots: readonly SkillRoot[]): Promise<void> {
298	    if (this.closing) return
299	    const projectRoots = new Map<string, SkillRoot[]>()
300	    const pending: Promise<void>[] = []
301	    for (const root of roots) {
302	      if (root.projectRoot === undefined) {
303	        pending.push(this.retainRoot(root, `shared:${root.path}`))
304	        continue
305	      }
306	      const grouped = projectRoots.get(root.projectRoot) ?? []
307	      grouped.push(root)
308	      projectRoots.set(root.projectRoot, grouped)
309	    }
310	    for (const [projectRoot, grouped] of projectRoots) {
311	      const owner = `project:${projectRoot}`
312	      this.projects.delete(projectRoot)
313	      const paths = new Set(grouped.map(root => root.path))
314	      this.projects.set(projectRoot, paths)
315	      for (const root of grouped) pending.push(this.retainRoot(root, owner))
316	    }
317	    let evictedProject = false
318	    while (this.projects.size > this.config.maxProjects) {
319	      const oldest = this.projects.entries().next()
320	      /* v8 ignore next -- the loop condition proves one project exists. */
321	      if (oldest.done) break
322	      const [projectRoot, paths] = oldest.value
323	      this.projects.delete(projectRoot)
324	      const owner = `project:${projectRoot}`
325	      for (const path of paths) pending.push(this.releaseRoot(path, owner))
326	      evictedProject = true
327	    }
328	    await Promise.all(pending)
329	    if (evictedProject) this.invalidate()
330	  }

405	  private async replaceWatcher(state: RootWatchState): Promise<void> {

436	  private async openStableWatcher(state: RootWatchState): Promise<WatchHandle | undefined> {
437	    while (!this.closing && state.owners.size > 0) {
438	      const mode = await resolveRootWatchMode(state.root.path, this.config.followSymlinks)

445	      /* v8 ignore next -- Covered by the same host path transition guard. */
446	      await this.closeWatcher(watcher)

448	    /* v8 ignore next -- The loop exits only when teardown wins between awaited probes. */

487	  private async openRootWatcher(state: RootWatchState, mode: Extract<RootWatchMode, { kind: 'root' }>): Promise<WatchHandle> {
488	    const watcher = chokidar.watch(mode.anchor, {
489	      // Chokidar owns late native fs.watch errors only for persistent watchers;
490	      // this provider's effect explicitly closes every handle at teardown.
491	      persistent: true,
492	      ignoreInitial: true,
493	      depth: 1,
494	      followSymlinks: this.config.followSymlinks,
495	      atomic: true,
496	      awaitWriteFinish: {
497	        stabilityThreshold: this.config.stabilityThresholdMs,
498	        pollInterval: this.config.pollIntervalMs,
499	      },
500	      usePolling: this.config.usePolling,
501	      interval: this.config.pollIntervalMs,
502	    })
503	    const handle: WatchHandle = {
504	      mode,
505	      close: () => watcher.close(),
506	    }
507	    let ready = false
508	    const readiness = Promise.withResolvers<undefined>()
509	    const signal = this.lifecycle.signal
510	    if (signal.aborted) {
511	      await this.closeWatcher(handle)
512	      signal.throwIfAborted()
513	    }
514	    const onAbort = (): void => { readiness.reject(signal.reason) }
515	    signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
516	    const onError = (error: unknown): void => {
517	      if (!ready) {
518	        readiness.reject(error)
519	        return
520	      }
521	      this.handleWatcherError(state, error)
522	    }
523	    watcher.on('error', onError)
524	    watcher.once('ready', () => {
525	      ready = true
526	      readiness.resolve(undefined)
527	    })
528	    for (const event of ['add', 'addDir', 'change', 'unlink', 'unlinkDir'] as const) {
529	      watcher.on(event, (path) => { this.handleWatchEvent(state, mode, event, path) })
530	    }
531	    try {
532	      await readiness.promise
533	    } catch (error) {
534	      await this.closeWatcher(handle)
535	      throw error
536	    } finally {
537	      signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
538	    }
539	    return handle
540	  }

625	async function resolveRootWatchMode(root: string, followSymlinks: boolean): Promise<RootWatchMode> {
626	  let candidate = root
627	  while (true) {
628	    try {
629	      const info = await stat(candidate)
630	      if (info.isDirectory()) {
631	        const preserveRootLink = candidate === root
632	          && !followSymlinks
633	          && (await lstat(candidate)).isSymbolicLink()
634	        const anchor = preserveRootLink ? resolve(candidate) : await canonicalizeWatchPath(candidate)
635	        if (candidate === root) return { kind: 'root', anchor }
636	        const firstSegment = relative(candidate, root).split(sep)[0]
637	        /* v8 ignore next -- candidate is a strict ancestor of root. */
638	        if (firstSegment === undefined || firstSegment.length === 0) return { kind: 'root', anchor }
639	        return { kind: 'ancestor', anchor, nextPath: join(anchor, firstSegment) }
640	      }
641	    } catch (error) {
642	      /* v8 ignore next -- Non-absence stat failures are platform/permission-specific and propagate as incomplete discovery. */
643	      if (!isAbsentPathError(error)) throw error
644	    }
645	    const parent = dirname(candidate)
646	    /* v8 ignore next -- Traversal reaches the existing filesystem root before this fallback. */
647	    if (parent === candidate) return { kind: 'ancestor', anchor: candidate, nextPath: root }
648	    candidate = parent
649	  }
650	}

658	function isRelevantWatchEvent(
659	  root: SkillRoot,
660	  event: SkillWatchEvent,
661	  path: string,
662	): boolean {
663	  const segments = containedSegments(root.path, path)
664	  if (segments === undefined) return false
665	  if (segments.length === 0) return event === 'addDir' || event === 'unlinkDir'
666	  if (root.skipSystem === true && segments[0] === '.system') return false
667	  if (segments.length === 1) {
668	    if (event === 'addDir' || event === 'unlinkDir') return true
669	    return segments[0]?.endsWith('.md') === true
670	  }
671	  return segments.length === 2
672	    && segments[1] === 'SKILL.md'
673	    && event !== 'addDir'
674	    && event !== 'unlinkDir'
675	}

678	  const segments = containedSegments(root.path, path)
679	  if (segments === undefined || segments.length === 0 || segments.length > 2) return false
680	  if (root.skipSystem === true && segments[0] === '.system') return false
681	  return segments.length === 1
682	    ? segments[0]?.endsWith('.md') === true
683	    : segments[1] === 'SKILL.md'

690	  return child.split(sep)

734	      description: parsed.description,
735	      ...parsed.whenToUse !== undefined ? { whenToUse: parsed.whenToUse } : {},
736	      invocation: parsed.invocation,
737	      provider,
738	      source: root.source,
739	      rank: root.rank,
740	      locator,
741	      resourceBase: { kind: 'directory', path: locator.directory },
742	      path: locator.path,
743	      ...parsed.metadata !== undefined ? { metadata: parsed.metadata } : {},

98	  if (typeof repetition !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(repetition) || repetition < 0) {

133	      const lookup = { cwd: exec.agent?.session.header.cwd, signal: exec.signal, scope: exec.agent }
134	      const summary = (await ctx.skills.list(lookup)).find(skill => skill.name === args.name)

142	      if (!skill) {

163	  // User-explicit skill invocation: a claimed user message whose first line

166	  // instructions context appended after every other injection — background
167	  // first (workspace rules, runtime policy, the catalog), the material the
168	  // model must act on last, closest to its answer. Registration order makes
169	  // that placement deterministic: this listener registers before the catalog

171	  // Only `source.kind === 'user'` messages are scanned — external text
172	  // cannot forge the gesture — and a token naming no user-invocable skill

174	  // namespace, resolved client-side before a line ever becomes a prompt).
175	  // This is the only entry point for `disable-model-invocation` skills; the

179	    next,
180	  ): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {

184	    if (names.length === 0) return decision
185	    signal.throwIfAborted()
186	    const lookup = { cwd: agent.session.header.cwd, signal, scope: agent }
187	    const injections: UserMessage[] = []
188	    for (const name of names) {
189	      const skill = await ctx.skills.get(name, lookup)
190	      signal.throwIfAborted()

192	      // gesture was never a claim this boundary recognizes. The check sits
193	      // on the loaded definition — the single lookup that produces what is
194	      // actually injected.
195	      if (skill === undefined || !isUserInvocable(skill)) continue
196	      const source: SkillInvocationSource = { kind: 'skill-invocation', name, form: 'instructions' }

198	        content: [{ type: 'text', text: renderSkillContent(skill) }],
199	        source,

202	    if (injections.length === 0) return decision

206	  // Register after the tool so reverse teardown removes guidance first. Exact definition
207	  // identity prevents a scoped shadow merely named `skill` from inheriting this catalog.
208	  //
209	  // The comparison is against the definition this plugin registered, not against
210	  // a lookup of its own name: `register()` files into the CALLING context's
211	  // scope, so a plugin mounted inside an agent preset registers for that agent
212	  // alone and an unscoped lookup correctly finds nothing.
213	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (
214	    { agent, signal },
215	    next,
216	  ): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
217	    const decision = await next()
218	    if (decision.kind === 'reject') return decision
219	    signal.throwIfAborted()
220	    const toolVisible = ctx.tools.get(skillTool.name, agent) === skillTool
221	    const snapshot = toolVisible
222	      ? await ctx.skills.snapshot({ cwd: agent.session.header.cwd, signal, scope: agent })
223	      : { skills: [], complete: true }
224	    signal.throwIfAborted()
225	    if (!snapshot.complete) return decision
226	    const skills = snapshot.skills.filter(isModelInvocable)
227	    const entries = catalogSourceEntries(skills, catalogDescriptionMaxLength)
228	    const digest = digestCatalogEntries(entries)
229	    const history = catalogHistory(agent)
230	    const existing = catalogMessage(decision.messages)
231	    if (history.visibleDigest === digest) {
232	      return existing === undefined
233	        ? decision
234	        : { kind: 'enter', messages: decision.messages.filter(message => message.id !== existing.message.id) }
235	    }
236	    if (existing !== undefined && digestCatalogEntries(existing.entries) === digest) return decision
237	    if (!history.published && skills.length === 0) {
238	      return existing === undefined
239	        ? decision
240	        : { kind: 'enter', messages: decision.messages.filter(message => message.id !== existing.message.id) }
241	    }
242	    const catalog = history.published
243	      ? renderCatalogUpdate(entries)
244	      : renderCatalogMessage(entries)
245	    return {
246	      kind: 'enter',
247	      messages: existing === undefined
248	        ? [...decision.messages, catalog]
249	        : decision.messages.map(message => message.id === existing.message.id ? catalog : message),
250	    }
251	  })

313	/**
314	 * Model-facing catalog lines, projected from the same entries the source records.
315	 * The pseudo-XML escaping belongs to this frame, not to the published fact, so it
316	 * is applied here and never stored. Names are `isSkillName`-validated and carry
317	 * no escapable character.
318	 */
319	function renderCatalogEntries(entries: SkillCatalogSource['entries']): string[] {
320	  return entries.map(entry => `- \`${entry.name}\`: ${escapeText(entry.description)}`)
321	}
322	
323	/**
324	 * Catalog identity over the durable entry list rather than the rendered prose.
325	 * The entries are what changes; the surrounding `<system-reminder>` framing is
326	 * written for the model and must not decide whether a republish is needed.
327	 */
328	function digestCatalogEntries(entries: SkillCatalogSource['entries']): string {
329	  // JSON per entry rather than a separator character: every separator is itself
330	  // a legal description character, so only quoting makes the boundary exact.
331	  const canonical = entries.map(entry => JSON.stringify([entry.name, entry.description])).join('\n')
332	  return createHash('sha256')
333	    .update(canonical)
334	    .digest('hex')
335	}
