The denied set for a role is not among them: which authorities an `implementer` may hold is a security invariant, not a deployment choice.

**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today.

**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read counterpart of the write and edit policy [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) contributes through the same event gate. It registers no service and declares no `Config`, because every deployment-varying value belongs to the barrier above: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim.

##### Exact error

```markdown
read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
```

**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member with `ignorable: true`, so a build that does not know the type still reads the log under the [version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md).

**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on `cordis_inspect`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.

**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.

##### Exact mount refusal

```markdown
agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
```

**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.

##### Exact guard denial

```markdown
"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
```

**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.

**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.

**The scope census.** Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`.

**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` reads `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.

**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must exist, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, be unwritable by that uid and its groups, and contain exactly the run's environment content hashes as the `environment/run` stamp carries them. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. On Windows the ownership and write tests read the ACL through the primitives `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` already owns. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation and the claim is refused.

**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's denied directories plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set immediately after the fixture overlay and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'tampered'`. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner records the run, issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task, and never calls `recordRun`, so no certificate can exist for that run. `foldTrajectory` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate that follows a `tampered` run.

**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.

## The isolation ladder

| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
|---|---|---|---|

# Agent Note: Content-addressed identity and the composition manifest event

Status: proposed

English | [中文](2026-09-05-composition-manifest.zh.md)

## Problem

Every identity in the harness names a slot rather than the bytes in it. A `ComponentId` is "derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order" ([`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md)), a skill is addressed by its kebab-case name, a prompt section and a tool by their registered names, a preset by its directory name, and a plugin by its package name. Editing a skill body in place leaves all of those addresses unchanged, so a leaderboard cannot separate the generation before the edit from the generation after it, a rollback has no earlier address to return to, and a decontamination check has nothing to key on — the failure the [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) records under its rejected "single mutable knowledge store" alternative and forbids in principle P5.

Nothing durable records which components a session had in play. The `request/header` event carries each epoch's assembled system prompt text and tool schemas, which is enough to replay a request and not enough to name what produced it: it carries no component identity, provenance, lineage, or registry layer; a skill body loaded through the `skill` tool reaches the transcript as a tool result and never the header; and a dynamic package mounted through [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) that registers no tool is invisible in it. The component registry itself is composition-time state that dies with the process, as [the component-registry seam note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) states outright.

Four consumers are blocked on that gap. [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) ships no `composition_hash`, `component_ids`, or `skills_used` field because no event supplies one. W4 stage 1's invariant — a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest fails — has no manifest to check against. The trajectory exporter can withhold a held-out environment but cannot tell a curated composition from one an agent mutated mid-session, so a synthesized skill body can reach a training set unannounced. And W4 stage 9's knowledge ledger has no address to mirror its entries against, which is what makes "a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence never counts as having been in play" enforceable rather than aspirational.

## Proposal

**One digest function, one address form.** [`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md) gains `ComponentDigest` (a `Branded<'ComponentDigest'>` from `dsh-brand`) and two pure functions: `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex of `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` ``, and `componentAddress(id, digest)` returns `` `${id}@${digest}` ``. The kind is inside the hashed bytes so two kinds whose canonical values coincide never share an address. The digest is the full 64 hex characters everywhere it is stored or compared, matching `environmentContentHashes` in [`dsh-environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md); truncating it for a card or a table is a presentation choice that never enters a log or the ledger. `ComponentDescriptor` gains a required `digest: ComponentDigest` and a required `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'`.

**Each producer owns its canonical value.** The registry ships no per-kind canonicalization for the same reason it ships no kind: each producer declares its `ComponentKindMap` member by declaration merging and exports the pure function that canonicalizes it, so a kind added later needs no change in the registry or in the manifest writer. The table below fixes the canonical value of every kind this note introduces.

**The registry becomes layered.** `ComponentRegistry` today is one flat `Map`, so it cannot answer "what does this agent see". It moves to `ScopedLayers` from `dsh-scope`, exactly as [`ctx.tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) and [`ctx.skills`](../../../../packages/skill/skill/README.md) already do: `register()` files into the calling context's scope, and `list({ kind, scope })` merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, the nearest layer's entry winning a duplicate id. A descriptor read back through a scope carries `layer: 'global' | 'agent'` — `global` when the winning registration sits in the global layer, `agent` when it sits in a layer of that agent's scope chain. A deeper chain still reads as `agent`, because a subagent writes its own manifest into its own session.

**The manifest writer reads one registry.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` at `packages/components/components-manifest/` injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else. On `agent/pre-step` it calls `next()` first, recomputes `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })` for the calling agent, compares the resulting `compositionSha256` with the last `composition/manifest` event in that session's log, and appends a new event through `agent.session.append()` only when the two differ — the shape [`dsh-budget-policy`](../../../../packages/guard/budget-policy/README.md) already uses to fold and append before a step opens. Recomputing rather than tracking incrementally is what keeps it correct across HMR disposal, a preset mounted after creation, and scope shadowing: the writer holds no subscription state that any of those three orderings could invalidate.

**Every other seam reaches the manifest through an adapter.** The one-adapter-per-seam rule [the component-registry note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) established is what keeps the writer from reading registries it does not own, and each adapter follows its seam's own change notification: `dsh-components-tools` follows `tools/change`, `dsh-components-prompt` follows `system-prompt/change`, `dsh-components-skills` follows `tools/result` for the `skill` tool, `dsh-components-presets` follows the `agent-preset/selected` Cordis event, and the shipped `dsh-components-subagents` already follows `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. One seam emits nothing today: the dynamic Cordis runner behind `tool-cordis` reports no change when a package is defined, run, stopped, or removed, so `dsh-cordis-host-runner` gains an unfiltered `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` Cordis event — `@mode emit`, not scope-filtered, so no scope-scan metadata applies — and `dsh-components-packages` follows it.

**A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed.** `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries without bodies, so registering every discoverable skill would need a body load per catalog entry per step and would still address a summary rather than the knowledge. `dsh-skill` therefore exports `skillDigest(definition)` over the loaded definition, the `skill` tool's canonical output value gains a `digest` field (absent from `renderSkillContent`, so the model-facing text is unchanged, and durable in `tool/result`), and `SkillInvocationSource` gains the same field so the user-explicit `/name` injection records it too. `dsh-components-skills` registers a `skill` component from either durable record through `exec.agent.ctx`, never by re-parsing the rendered `<skill_content>` block. Skills that were reachable but never loaded stay out of the manifest; the catalog they came from is already durable as the `skill-catalog` message source.

## What each kind hashes

| Kind | Canonical value | Basis | Producer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skill` | `[name, description, whenToUse ?? null, invocation.modelInvocable, invocation.userInvocable, metadata ?? null, content]` from the loaded `SkillDefinition` | content | `dsh-components-skills`, over `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill` |
| `prompt-section` | `[name, order, complete === true, text]` when `PromptSection.text` is a string; `[name, order, complete === true, null]` when it is a provider evaluated per assembly | content, else registration | `dsh-components-prompt` |
| `tool` | the model-facing `ToolSchema` as `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` projects it: name, description, parameter schema, output schema, in the registry's own field order | content | `dsh-components-tools` |
| `preset` | `[id, trust, rows]`, where `rows` is the preset's composition after `include` resolution as `[id, name, config, disabled]` per row, with every `name` that resolves to a path rewritten relative to the preset directory | content | `dsh-components-presets` |
| `plugin` | `[packageName, version, patchLayerSha256]`, the version from the resolved package manifest and `patchLayerSha256` the SHA-256 over the ordered `cordis.patch.yml` rows of the bundles in force | content | `dsh-components-packages`, over `ctx.loader.entries()` |
| `dynamic-package` | `[pluginId, packageId, hostSource, clientSource]` from `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.inspectPlugin(agent, pluginId)` | content | `dsh-components-packages` |
| `agent-provider` | `[provider]` | registration | `dsh-components-subagents` |

A digest never covers the viewing scope, the working directory, a wall-clock time, an absolute path (`SkillDefinition.path`, `SkillResourceBase`'s directory, `AgentPreset.path`), a discovery `source` or `rank`, a provider name, or any value a registry computes per assembly. Two hosts that discovered the same skill under different roots, and the same body re-registered through a different provider, therefore address identically; one byte changed in a skill body, a tool parameter description, a static prompt section, or a preset row moves the digest. A `registration`-basis digest addresses the registration and not the bytes the model saw, which is the honest statement for a section whose text is a function of the assembly; the rendered bytes stay where they already are, in `request/header`.

## The `composition/manifest` event

`dsh-components-manifest` declaration-merges one member into `SessionEventMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types`. It is **log-only** and carries no `@mode` tag: a session log event has no dispatch mode, it rides the single `session/event` emit, and `gen-persistence-catalog` rejects the tag outright — the repo's `@mode` and payload-`@param` rules govern the Cordis bus event this note adds, not this one. It is **required-on-read**, without the envelope's `ignorable: true` marker, because every consumer below keys a refusal on it: a build that cannot interpret the type would otherwise fold a scoreboard row and write an export line for a session it cannot prove was unquarantined ([the version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)). Its payload fields, each carrying its own JSDoc so [the generated catalog](../../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) documents them:

- `kind: 'composition/manifest'` and `version: 1`, the self-declared payload version the environment stamp also carries.
- `reason`: why this manifest was written — `'session-start'`, `'preset-mounted'`, `'skill-loaded'`, `'tools-changed'`, `'prompt-changed'`, or `'package-mounted'`, decided by which kinds changed since the previous manifest.
- `presetId`: the preset the agent runs, resolved through `resolveSessionPreset()`; absent when the deployment composes none.
- `components`: one entry per component in play, ordered by `id`, each `{ id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis }`.
- `compositionSha256`: SHA-256 over the ordered `id@digest` addresses joined by newlines — the deduplication key and the `composition_hash` the scoreboard row wants.
- `dynamicPackagesMounted`: whether any entry has kind `dynamic-package`.
- `synthesized`: the ids of every entry whose `provenance` is `synthesized`, in the same order.

The four-goal note's sketch lists a `seq` field; the envelope already carries `seq`, so the payload does not repeat it. The first manifest is appended before the session's first `request/header`, because `agent/pre-step` runs before the step assembles its request and the preset has already settled by then — a preset chosen after creation commits `agent-preset/selected` while the session is still blank. Every later change to the set in play produces the next differing manifest at the next step, which is the first step whose model request that change can reach.

## Quarantine

A session is quarantined when its latest manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted` or a non-empty `synthesized`, and equally when its log carries no manifest at all: a session that cannot prove what was in play is exactly as unusable as one that mounted code an agent wrote. `SessionFacts.identity` in [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) gains a `composition` group folded from the latest manifest — `compositionSha256`, the entry count, `presetId`, `dynamicPackagesMounted`, and `synthesized` — plus `skillsUsed`, the `id@digest` addresses of every `skill` entry any manifest of the session named. Its `./invariant` companion gains one relation beside the three it checks today: for every `tool/result` of the `skill` tool carrying a digest, some `composition/manifest` at or before that event's `seq` names a `skill` component with that digest, and a result whose digest appears in no manifest is reported as a record disagreeing with its own log. [`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) gains `includeQuarantined?: boolean` on `TrajectoryExportRequest` and a `quarantined` count on `TrajectoryExportReport`, symmetric with `includeHeldOut` and `heldOut`: absent, the export refuses every quarantined session and accounts for it in the count rather than dropping it silently. The complementary quarantine — a Harness Engineer proposal that touches an evaluator-owned path — belongs to W1 stage 7 and stays there.

## The knowledge ledger

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive` at `packages/improvement/archive/` (`ctx.archive`) holds the cross-session records over [`ctx.storage.domain`](../../../../packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md), through a `defineDomain` spec whose record schemas are zod, routed to whichever backend the deployment configures. Two tables: `variants`, keyed by the `HarnessVariant` id (base commit plus patch-set hash) with the fields the four-goal note fixes — `parent`, `operator`, `patch`, `scores`, `evaluations[]`, `children[]`, `status`, `proposer`; and `generations`, keyed by `id@digest` with `componentId`, `digest`, `kind`, `provenance`, `lineage` (the parent's address, absent for a root), `evidenceSessions[]`, `results`, and `status`. A mutation mints a new row rather than rewriting one, so a generation's bytes and its address never diverge.

`status` is `alive`, `dominated`, `promoted`, or `deprecated`. `alive` is evaluated or newly minted and still eligible for parent sampling; `dominated` lost to another generation of its lineage on every measured cell and stays sampleable and auditable, never deleted, which is the archive semantics the four-goal note's rejected best-only alternative exists to preserve; `promoted` carries the `PromotionDecision` that moved it into curated source; `deprecated` is what the department scoreboard writes once a paired present-versus-absent delta has stayed at or below zero over the configured number of runs. Lineage is stored on both ends — `lineage` on the child for the auditor walking up, `children[]` on the parent for the sampler's `1/(1+children)` weight — and a status change appends a revision rather than removing a row.

The ledger's `./invariant` companion owns the manifest-versus-ledger relation, an assertion over mutable data against the authoritative event stream the [package invariant rules](../../../../packages/AGENTS.md) require: for every generation row, each session named in `evidenceSessions` must carry a `composition/manifest` whose `components` hold that exact `id@digest`. A row that names an evidence session with no matching occurrence is reported and never counts as having been in play, so a promotion cannot rest on a session the component was not actually composed into.

## Alternatives considered

**Derive the manifest from `request/header`.** The header already records the assembled system prompt and every tool schema of each epoch, so a fold over it would need no new event. It is rejected because the header carries rendered text and no identity: provenance, lineage, and layer are absent, a loaded skill body never reaches it, and a dynamic package that registers no tool leaves it unchanged — precisely the three cases the quarantine has to catch.

**Keep the registry composition-time only, with no session event.** `ctx.components` is already the inventory, so a consumer could read it live. It is rejected because every consumer here reads persisted logs after the fact — the scorekeeper folds them, the exporter writes from them, the ledger invariant checks against them — and composition-time truth dies with the process.

**One manifest per session, written at creation.** A single record would be smaller and simpler to fold. It is rejected because a skill load, a preset switch, and a dynamic mount all change the set mid-session, and a start-of-session record would report a clean composition for exactly the sessions the quarantine exists to flag.

**Hash each component's rendered contribution.** Hashing what the model actually received would tie the digest to the bytes in the transcript. It is rejected because rendering depends on the working directory, the wall clock, and the viewing scope, so two identical compositions on two hosts would address differently and decontamination would key on noise; `request/header` already owns the rendered bytes, and the manifest owns identity.

**Put the per-kind canonicalization in the manifest writer.** One switch over kinds inside the writer would avoid an adapter per seam. It is rejected because the writer would then have to know every kind, which is the coupling `ComponentKindMap`'s declaration merging removes, and a kind added downstream could not be digested at all.

**A monotonic version counter per component instead of a content address.** A `skill@3` label is shorter and human-readable. It is rejected for the reason the four-goal note's "single mutable knowledge store" alternative was: a counter is authored rather than derived, so two hosts that refine the same body disagree on the number, a body restored from an ancestor gets a new number instead of its old address, and no consumer can verify the label against the bytes.

**A `components/change` event with an incremental writer.** Mirroring `tools/change` would let the writer maintain the manifest between steps instead of recomputing it. It is rejected because recomputation is one registry read and one hash per step and cannot be wrong, while an incremental writer would have to stay correct across HMR disposal, preset remounts, and scope shadowing; no consumer in this note needs a change notification, so the event is not added until one does.

**The ledger as session events rather than storage.** Recording generations in the log would keep everything on one plane. It is rejected because a ledger spans sessions and outlives every one of them, and because the manifest-versus-ledger invariant needs two planes to be a real check: an entry that is itself a session event could not be contradicted by the session events it cites.

## Acceptance criteria

- A Loader-booted composition at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/` appends one `composition/manifest` before the session's first `request/header`; the event names the preset id, carries one entry per component in play with a `digest`, `provenance`, `layer`, and `digestBasis`, and its `compositionSha256` equals a recomputation from the ordered `id@digest` addresses in the persisted log.
- In the same fixture, the agent calls the `skill` tool once; a second manifest follows with `reason: 'skill-loaded'`, one added `skill` entry whose digest equals `skillDigest()` over that body, and a different `compositionSha256`. A step that changes nothing appends no third event.
- Two runs of that fixture under different temporary workspace roots and different `DSH_HOME` values produce byte-identical `compositionSha256` values, proving absolute paths, discovery roots, and timestamps are outside every digest.
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` runs the same composition twice with one byte of the skill body changed between the runs; exactly one entry's digest differs, `compositionSha256` differs, and every other entry is unchanged.
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-quarantine/` composes `tool-cordis`, defines and runs a dynamic package, and proves the next manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted: true` with the package's id in `synthesized`; the trajectory export then withholds that session and counts it as `quarantined`, and the same export with `includeQuarantined` writes it.
- A keyless unit test over a synthetic log proves the scorekeeper invariant reports a `skill` tool result whose digest appears in no preceding manifest, and accepts the same result once a manifest names it; a second proves a session with no manifest at all folds to a quarantined record rather than a clean one.
- A keyless unit test in `packages/improvement/archive/tests/` proves the ledger invariant reports a generation row whose evidence session carries no manifest occurrence of its `id@digest`, and accepts the row once one exists.
- The persisted-log snapshot suite `examples/headless-agent` owns records the manifest events for the scenario that composes the manifest writer; the event is log-only and changes no model-visible text, so the required coverage is the persisted log rather than a transcript re-record ([testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md)).

## Rollout

1. `dsh-components`: the `ComponentDigest` brand, `componentDigest()` and `componentAddress()`, the required `digest` and `digestBasis` on `ComponentDescriptor`, and the `ScopedLayers` layering with `list({ kind, scope })` and the derived `layer`. Updates `dsh-components-subagents` and `dsh-command-components`, [`docs/subsystems/components.md`](../../../../docs/subsystems/components.md), and the three package READMEs.
2. The composition-time adapters and their canonical values: `dsh-components-tools`, `dsh-components-prompt`, and `dsh-components-presets` at `packages/components/`, each following its seam's existing change event.
3. `dsh-components-manifest`: the `composition/manifest` declaration, the `agent/pre-step` writer with `compositionSha256` deduplication, the regenerated `known-event-types.ts` and persistence catalog, and the `composition-manifest` fixture.
4. Skill generations: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill`, the `digest` field on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource`, `dsh-components-skills`, and the mutation fixture.
5. Dynamic packages: `cordis/dynamic-changed` on `dsh-cordis-host-runner`, `dsh-components-packages` over `ctx.loader.entries()` and the dynamic runner, and the quarantine fixture.
6. Quarantine consumers: the `composition` group and `skillsUsed` on `SessionFacts`, the scorekeeper invariant relation, and `includeQuarantined` with the `quarantined` count in `dsh-trajectories`.
7. `dsh-archive`: the domain spec, the `variants` and `generations` tables, the four statuses and their transitions, the two-ended lineage edges, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant.

## Risks

A `registration`-basis digest cannot detect a change in what a provider-evaluated prompt section produced, so two runs whose dynamic sections differed share an address. `request/header` carries those bytes and a comparison that needs them must read it; a leaderboard keyed on the manifest alone will pool the two.

A `plugin` digest keys on package name and version, and every workspace package here is `0.0.1`, so a source edit does not move it. `HarnessVariant`'s base commit plus patch-set hash is what addresses harness source, and a comparison that keys on plugin digests alone will pool generations of the same package.

The manifest names components, not their transitive effects. An MCP server whose remote tool descriptions change without a re-registration, or a skill whose body references a file that changed, keeps its digest; only what the canonical value covers is addressed.

Required-on-read means a build that does not know `composition/manifest` refuses a log containing it. That is the intended trade — the alternative is a build silently treating a quarantined session as clean — and it is affordable only under the pre-release stance in the root [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md).

A composition that churns its visible tool set every step writes one manifest per step. Deduplication by `compositionSha256` keeps a stable composition to exactly one event, and a churning one is paying for a real change in what the model can call, but a scoped restriction toggled per step would inflate a log with events no consumer distinguishes.

# Agent Note: 内容寻址的身份与组合清单事件

Status: proposed

[English](2026-09-05-composition-manifest.md) | 中文

## Problem

harness 中的每一个身份指向的都是一个位置，而不是位置里的字节。`ComponentId`"由它的 kind 与拥有它的 seam 的稳定名称推导而来，绝不来自挂载顺序"（[`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md)），skill（技能）由它的 kebab-case 名称寻址，prompt 段落与工具由它们的注册名寻址，preset 由它的目录名寻址，插件由它的包名寻址。就地修改一个 skill 的正文不会改变上述任何一个地址，于是排行榜无法把修改前的代际与修改后的代际分开，回滚没有更早的地址可以返回，去污染检查也没有可以作为键的东西——这正是[四目标工作流 note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) 在它被否决的"单一可变知识存储"备选方案中记录的失败，也是它的原则 P5 明令禁止的。

没有任何持久记录说明一个会话实际让哪些组件在场。`request/header` 事件承载每个 epoch 组装出的系统提示词文本与工具 schema，这足以重放一次请求，却不足以指名是什么产生了它：它不承载组件身份、provenance、lineage 或注册表层级；通过 `skill` 工具加载的 skill 正文以工具结果进入转录，永远不会进入 header；而通过 [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) 挂载、且没有注册任何工具的动态包在其中完全不可见。组件注册表本身是随进程消亡的组合期状态，[组件注册表 seam note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) 已经明确这样陈述。

有四个消费方卡在这个缺口上。[`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) 没有发布 `composition_hash`、`component_ids` 或 `skills_used` 字段，因为没有事件提供它们。W4 阶段 1 的不变式——skill 结果的摘要若不在清单中即失败——没有可供核对的清单。轨迹导出器可以扣下一个 held-out 环境，却无法把一个 curated 组合与一个 agent（智能体）在会话中途变异过的组合区分开，于是一个合成的 skill 正文可以不加声明地进入训练集。而 W4 阶段 9 的知识 ledger 没有可供其条目对照的地址，而正是这种对照让"一条在清单中没有对应出现的 ledger 条目从不算作曾经在场"成为可执行的规则而非愿望。

## Proposal

**一个摘要函数，一种地址形式。** [`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md) 新增 `ComponentDigest`（来自 `dsh-brand` 的 `Branded<'ComponentDigest'>`）与两个纯函数：`componentDigest(kind, canonical)` 返回 `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` `` 的小写 SHA-256 十六进制值，`componentAddress(id, digest)` 返回 `` `${id}@${digest}` ``。kind 被包含在被哈希的字节内，因此两个规范值恰好相同的 kind 绝不会共享同一个地址。摘要在任何被存储或被比较的位置都是完整的 64 个十六进制字符，与 [`dsh-environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md) 中的 `environmentContentHashes` 一致；为卡片或表格截短它是一种呈现选择，永远不会进入日志或 ledger。`ComponentDescriptor` 新增必填的 `digest: ComponentDigest` 与必填的 `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'`。

**每个生产者拥有自己的规范值。** 注册表不发布任何按 kind 的规范化逻辑，理由与它不发布任何 kind 相同：每个生产者通过声明合并声明自己的 `ComponentKindMap` 成员，并导出把它规范化的纯函数，于是后来新增的 kind 无需改动注册表或清单写入方。下面的表格固定了本 note 引入的每个 kind 的规范值。

**注册表变为分层。** 今天的 `ComponentRegistry` 是一个扁平 `Map`，因此无法回答"这个 agent 看到了什么"。它改用 `dsh-scope` 的 `ScopedLayers`，与 [`ctx.tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) 和 [`ctx.skills`](../../../../packages/skill/skill/README.md) 今天的做法完全一致：`register()` 归档到调用上下文的作用域中，`list({ kind, scope })` 把全局层与查看作用域的链合并，最近的层的条目赢得同名 id。经由某个作用域读回的描述符携带 `layer: 'global' | 'agent'`——胜出的注册位于全局层时为 `global`，位于该 agent 作用域链的某一层时为 `agent`。更深的链仍读作 `agent`，因为子 agent 在自己的会话里写自己的清单。

**清单写入方只读一个注册表。** 位于 `packages/components/components-manifest/` 的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` 注入 `agents` 与 `components`，仅此而已。在 `agent/pre-step` 上它先调用 `next()`，为调用中的 agent 重算 `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })`，把得到的 `compositionSha256` 与该会话日志中最后一条 `composition/manifest` 事件比较，仅在两者不同时通过 `agent.session.append()` 追加一条新事件——正是 [`dsh-budget-policy`](../../../../packages/guard/budget-policy/README.md) 已经在步骤开启前用于折叠与追加的形状。选择重算而非增量跟踪，正是让它在 HMR 释放、创建后才挂载的 preset 以及作用域遮蔽这三种顺序下都保持正确的原因：写入方不持有任何这三者可能失效的订阅状态。

**其他每个 seam 都通过适配器抵达清单。**[组件注册表 note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) 确立的"每个 seam 一个适配器包"规则，正是让写入方不必读取自己不拥有的注册表的原因，而每个适配器跟随它自己 seam 的变更通知：`dsh-components-tools` 跟随 `tools/change`，`dsh-components-prompt` 跟随 `system-prompt/change`，`dsh-components-skills` 跟随 `skill` 工具的 `tools/result`，`dsh-components-presets` 跟随 `agent-preset/selected` Cordis 事件，已发布的 `dsh-components-subagents` 则已经跟随 `subagent/provider-added` 与 `subagent/provider-removed`。有一个 seam 今天什么都不发出：`tool-cordis` 背后的动态 Cordis 运行器在一个包被定义、运行、停止或移除时不报告任何变更，因此 `dsh-cordis-host-runner` 新增一个不过滤的 `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` Cordis 事件——`@mode emit`，不按作用域过滤，因此不适用作用域扫描元数据——并由 `dsh-components-packages` 跟随它。

**skill 在其正文被加载后才算在场，而不是被列出后。** `ctx.skills.list()` 返回不含正文的摘要，因此把每个可发现的 skill 都注册进来，将需要每步为每个目录条目加载一次正文，而且寻址的仍是摘要而非知识。因此 `dsh-skill` 导出针对已加载定义的 `skillDigest(definition)`，`skill` 工具的规范输出值新增 `digest` 字段（不出现在 `renderSkillContent` 中，因此面向模型的文本不变，并在 `tool/result` 中持久化），`SkillInvocationSource` 也新增同一字段，使用户显式的 `/name` 注入同样有记录。`dsh-components-skills` 通过 `exec.agent.ctx` 从这两种持久记录中的任一种注册一个 `skill` 组件，绝不重新解析已渲染的 `<skill_content>` 块。可达但从未加载的 skill 不进入清单；它们所来自的目录已经作为 `skill-catalog` 消息来源持久化。

## What each kind hashes

| Kind | 规范值 | 依据 | 生产者 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skill` | 来自已加载 `SkillDefinition` 的 `[name, description, whenToUse ?? null, invocation.modelInvocable, invocation.userInvocable, metadata ?? null, content]` | content | `dsh-components-skills`，经由 `dsh-skill` 的 `skillDigest()` |
| `prompt-section` | `PromptSection.text` 为字符串时是 `[name, order, complete === true, text]`；它是按每次组装求值的提供者时是 `[name, order, complete === true, null]` | content，否则 registration | `dsh-components-prompt` |
| `tool` | `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` 投影出的面向模型 `ToolSchema`：名称、描述、参数 schema、输出 schema，按注册表自身的字段顺序 | content | `dsh-components-tools` |
| `preset` | `[id, trust, rows]`，其中 `rows` 是 `include` 解析后该 preset 的组合，每行为 `[id, name, config, disabled]`，且每个解析为路径的 `name` 都改写为相对 preset 目录的路径 | content | `dsh-components-presets` |
| `plugin` | `[packageName, version, patchLayerSha256]`，version 来自解析出的包清单，`patchLayerSha256` 是在场 bundle 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 有序行的 SHA-256 | content | `dsh-components-packages`，经由 `ctx.loader.entries()` |
| `dynamic-package` | 来自 `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.inspectPlugin(agent, pluginId)` 的 `[pluginId, packageId, hostSource, clientSource]` | content | `dsh-components-packages` |
| `agent-provider` | `[provider]` | registration | `dsh-components-subagents` |

摘要从不覆盖查看作用域、工作目录、挂钟时间、绝对路径（`SkillDefinition.path`、`SkillResourceBase` 的目录、`AgentPreset.path`）、发现用的 `source` 或 `rank`、提供者名称，或任何注册表按每次组装计算出的值。因此，在不同根目录下发现同一个 skill 的两台主机，以及经由不同提供者重新注册的同一份正文，寻址结果相同；而 skill 正文、工具参数描述、静态 prompt 段落或 preset 行中任何一个字节的改变都会移动摘要。`registration` 依据的摘要寻址的是注册本身而非模型看到的字节，这对于文本是组装的函数的段落而言是诚实的陈述；已渲染的字节仍留在它们本来所在的位置，即 `request/header`。

## The `composition/manifest` event

`dsh-components-manifest` 向 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types` 中的 `SessionEventMap` 声明合并一个成员。它是**纯日志**的，且不携带 `@mode` 标签：会话日志事件没有派发模式，它搭乘单一的 `session/event` emit，而 `gen-persistence-catalog` 会直接拒绝该标签——仓库的 `@mode` 与载荷 `@param` 规则管辖的是本 note 新增的那个 Cordis 总线事件，而不是这一个。它是**读取时必需**的，不带信封的 `ignorable: true` 标记，因为下文每个消费方都把一次拒绝挂在它上面：否则一个无法解释该类型的构建，会为一个它无法证明未被隔离的会话折叠出记分板行并写出导出行（[版本机制](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)）。它的载荷字段各自携带自己的 JSDoc，以便[生成的目录](../../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md)记录它们：

- `kind: 'composition/manifest'` 与 `version: 1`，即环境 stamp 同样携带的自声明载荷版本。
- `reason`：这条清单为何被写出——`'session-start'`、`'preset-mounted'`、`'skill-loaded'`、`'tools-changed'`、`'prompt-changed'` 或 `'package-mounted'`，由自上一条清单以来哪些 kind 发生变化决定。
- `presetId`：该 agent 运行所依据的 preset，经 `resolveSessionPreset()` 解析；部署未组合任何 preset 时缺省。
- `components`：在场的每个组件一条条目，按 `id` 排序，每条为 `{ id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis }`。
- `compositionSha256`：对有序 `id@digest` 地址以换行连接后的 SHA-256——去重键，也是记分板行想要的 `composition_hash`。
- `dynamicPackagesMounted`：是否存在 kind 为 `dynamic-package` 的条目。
- `synthesized`：`provenance` 为 `synthesized` 的每条条目的 id，顺序相同。

四目标 note 的草稿列出了一个 `seq` 字段；信封已经携带 `seq`，因此载荷不重复它。第一条清单在会话的第一条 `request/header` 之前追加，因为 `agent/pre-step` 在步骤组装其请求之前运行，而 preset 到那时已经稳定——创建之后选定的 preset 会在会话仍为空白时提交 `agent-preset/selected`。此后每一次在场集合的变化都会在下一步产生下一条不同的清单，而那一步正是该变化能够抵达的第一个模型请求。

## Quarantine

当一个会话最新的清单报告 `dynamicPackagesMounted` 或非空的 `synthesized` 时，它被隔离；当它的日志根本没有任何清单时同样被隔离：一个无法证明什么在场的会话，与一个挂载了 agent 自己编写的代码的会话同样不可用。[`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) 的 `SessionFacts.identity` 新增一个从最新清单折叠出的 `composition` 分组——`compositionSha256`、条目数量、`presetId`、`dynamicPackagesMounted` 与 `synthesized`——外加 `skillsUsed`，即该会话任何一条清单指名过的每个 `skill` 条目的 `id@digest` 地址。它的 `./invariant` 伴生插件在今天检查的三条关系之外新增一条：对于携带摘要的每一条 `skill` 工具 `tool/result`，在该事件 `seq` 之前或同处必须有某条 `composition/manifest` 指名一个带该摘要的 `skill` 组件，而摘要不出现在任何清单中的结果会被报告为记录与自身日志不一致。[`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) 在 `TrajectoryExportRequest` 上新增 `includeQuarantined?: boolean`，并在 `TrajectoryExportReport` 上新增 `quarantined` 计数，与 `includeHeldOut` 和 `heldOut` 对称：缺省时导出拒绝每一个被隔离的会话，并把它计入该计数而不是无声丢弃。互补的那种隔离——Harness Engineer 的提案触及评估方拥有的路径——属于 W1 阶段 7，仍留在那里。

## The knowledge ledger

位于 `packages/improvement/archive/` 的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive`（`ctx.archive`）在 [`ctx.storage.domain`](../../../../packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md) 之上持有跨会话记录，通过一份记录 schema 为 zod 的 `defineDomain` 规格，路由到部署所配置的任一后端。两张表：`variants`，以 `HarnessVariant` id（基线提交加补丁集哈希）为键，字段由四目标 note 固定——`parent`、`operator`、`patch`、`scores`、`evaluations[]`、`children[]`、`status`、`proposer`；以及 `generations`，以 `id@digest` 为键，带 `componentId`、`digest`、`kind`、`provenance`、`lineage`（父代的地址，根代缺省）、`evidenceSessions[]`、`results` 与 `status`。一次变异铸造一条新行而不是改写既有行，因此一个代际的字节与它的地址永不背离。

`status` 为 `alive`、`dominated`、`promoted` 或 `deprecated`。`alive` 表示已评估或新铸造且仍可被父代采样；`dominated` 表示在每个被测量的单元格上都输给了同一 lineage 的另一个代际，仍可被采样与审计，永不删除，这正是四目标 note 被否决的"只保留最优"备选方案所要保住的档案语义；`promoted` 携带把它移入 curated 源码的那条 `PromotionDecision`；`deprecated` 是部门记分板在成对的"在场对不在场"增量于所配置的运行次数内始终小于等于零之后写下的状态。lineage 在两端都被存储——子代上的 `lineage` 供向上追溯的审计者使用，父代上的 `children[]` 供采样器的 `1/(1+children)` 权重使用——而状态变化追加一次修订而不是移除一行。

ledger 的 `./invariant` 伴生插件拥有清单对 ledger 的关系，这是[包不变式规则](../../../../packages/AGENTS.md)所要求的、针对可变数据与权威事件流的断言：对于每一条代际行，`evidenceSessions` 中指名的每个会话都必须携带一条 `composition/manifest`，其 `components` 中含有那个确切的 `id@digest`。一条指名了没有对应出现的证据会话的行会被报告，且从不算作曾经在场，于是一次晋升不可能建立在该组件实际并未被组合进去的会话之上。

## Alternatives considered

**从 `request/header` 推导清单。** header 已经记录每个 epoch 组装出的系统提示词与每个工具 schema，因此在它之上折叠不需要新事件。这被否决，因为 header 承载的是已渲染的文本而非身份：provenance、lineage 与层级都缺席，已加载的 skill 正文永不进入其中，而一个不注册任何工具的动态包不会改变它——恰恰是隔离必须抓住的那三种情形。

**让注册表只停留在组合期，不新增会话事件。** `ctx.components` 已经是那份清单，因此消费方可以在运行时读取它。这被否决，因为这里的每个消费方都在事后读取已持久化日志——记分板折叠它们，导出器从它们写出，ledger 不变式对照它们检查——而组合期真相随进程消亡。

**每会话一条清单，在创建时写出。** 单条记录更小、也更容易折叠。这被否决，因为一次 skill 加载、一次 preset 切换与一次动态挂载都会在会话中途改变在场集合，而创建时的记录恰恰会为隔离本该标记的那些会话报告一个干净的组合。

**哈希每个组件已渲染的贡献。** 哈希模型实际收到的内容，会把摘要与转录中的字节绑定在一起。这被否决，因为渲染依赖工作目录、挂钟时间与查看作用域，于是两台主机上两个完全相同的组合会寻址到不同结果，去污染将以噪声为键；`request/header` 已经拥有已渲染的字节，而清单拥有身份。

**把按 kind 的规范化放进清单写入方。** 写入方内部的一个 kind 分支可以省去每个 seam 一个适配器。这被否决，因为写入方将不得不知道每一个 kind，而这正是 `ComponentKindMap` 的声明合并所消除的耦合，并且下游新增的 kind 将根本无法被摘要。

**用每个组件单调递增的版本计数器代替内容地址。** `skill@3` 这样的标签更短、也更便于人读。这被否决，理由与四目标 note 的"单一可变知识存储"备选方案相同：计数器是被撰写而非被推导的，于是精炼同一份正文的两台主机对数字并不一致，从祖先恢复的正文会拿到一个新数字而不是它原有的地址，而且没有消费方能够拿标签去核对字节。

**新增 `components/change` 事件并配一个增量写入方。** 仿照 `tools/change` 可以让写入方在步骤之间维护清单，而不是重算它。这被否决，因为重算只是每步一次注册表读取与一次哈希，且不可能出错，而增量写入方必须在 HMR 释放、preset 重新挂载与作用域遮蔽下都保持正确；本 note 中没有任何消费方需要变更通知，因此在出现一个之前不新增该事件。

**把 ledger 做成会话事件而非存储。** 把代际记录进日志可以把一切保留在同一个平面上。这被否决，因为 ledger 跨越会话并且比其中任何一个都活得更久，也因为清单对 ledger 的不变式需要两个平面才成其为真正的检查：一条本身就是会话事件的条目，无法被它所引用的会话事件所反驳。

## Acceptance criteria

- 位于 `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/` 的一个由 Loader 启动的组合，在会话的第一条 `request/header` 之前追加一条 `composition/manifest`；该事件指名 preset id，为在场的每个组件携带一条带 `digest`、`provenance`、`layer` 与 `digestBasis` 的条目，且其 `compositionSha256` 等于从已持久化日志中有序 `id@digest` 地址重算出的值。
- 在同一 fixture 中，agent 调用一次 `skill` 工具；随后出现第二条清单，`reason: 'skill-loaded'`，新增一条 `skill` 条目，其摘要等于对该正文的 `skillDigest()`，且 `compositionSha256` 不同。一个什么都没改变的步骤不追加第三条事件。
- 该 fixture 在不同临时工作区根目录与不同 `DSH_HOME` 值下的两次运行产生逐字节相同的 `compositionSha256`，证明绝对路径、发现根目录与时间戳都在每个摘要之外。
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` 以同一组合运行两次，两次之间改变 skill 正文的一个字节；恰好有一条条目的摘要不同，`compositionSha256` 不同，其余每条条目都未改变。
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-quarantine/` 组合 `tool-cordis`，定义并运行一个动态包，并证明下一条清单报告 `dynamicPackagesMounted: true` 且该包的 id 出现在 `synthesized` 中；随后轨迹导出扣下该会话并把它计为 `quarantined`，而同一次导出带上 `includeQuarantined` 时会写出它。
- 一个针对合成日志的无密钥单元测试证明记分板不变式会报告摘要不出现在任何在先清单中的 `skill` 工具结果，并在某条清单指名它之后接受同一结果；第二个测试证明一个完全没有清单的会话折叠为被隔离的记录而不是干净的记录。
- `packages/improvement/archive/tests/` 中的一个无密钥单元测试证明 ledger 不变式会报告证据会话中没有其 `id@digest` 清单出现的代际行，并在这样的出现存在之后接受该行。
- `examples/headless-agent` 所拥有的持久化日志快照套件记录组合了清单写入方的那个场景的清单事件；该事件是纯日志的，不改变任何面向模型的文本，因此所需的覆盖是持久化日志而不是重新录制转录（[测试策略](../../../../docs/testing.md)）。

## Rollout

1. `dsh-components`：`ComponentDigest` 品牌类型、`componentDigest()` 与 `componentAddress()`、`ComponentDescriptor` 上必填的 `digest` 与 `digestBasis`，以及带 `list({ kind, scope })` 与派生 `layer` 的 `ScopedLayers` 分层。更新 `dsh-components-subagents` 与 `dsh-command-components`、[`docs/subsystems/components.md`](../../../../docs/subsystems/components.md) 以及三个包 README。
2. 组合期适配器及其规范值：`packages/components/` 下的 `dsh-components-tools`、`dsh-components-prompt` 与 `dsh-components-presets`，各自跟随它所属 seam 已有的变更事件。
3. `dsh-components-manifest`：`composition/manifest` 声明、带 `compositionSha256` 去重的 `agent/pre-step` 写入方、重新生成的 `known-event-types.ts` 与持久化目录，以及 `composition-manifest` fixture。
4. skill 代际：`dsh-skill` 中的 `skillDigest()`、`skill` 工具规范值与 `SkillInvocationSource` 上的 `digest` 字段、`dsh-components-skills`，以及变异 fixture。
5. 动态包：`dsh-cordis-host-runner` 上的 `cordis/dynamic-changed`、经由 `ctx.loader.entries()` 与动态运行器的 `dsh-components-packages`，以及隔离 fixture。
6. 隔离消费方：`SessionFacts` 上的 `composition` 分组与 `skillsUsed`、记分板不变式关系，以及 `dsh-trajectories` 中的 `includeQuarantined` 与 `quarantined` 计数。
7. `dsh-archive`：领域规格、`variants` 与 `generations` 两张表、四种状态及其转换、两端存储的 lineage 边，以及清单对 ledger 的不变式。

## Risks

`registration` 依据的摘要无法察觉一个按组装求值的 prompt 段落产出内容的变化，因此两次动态段落不同的运行共享同一个地址。`request/header` 承载那些字节，需要它们的比较必须去读它；仅以清单为键的排行榜会把这两者混在一起。

`plugin` 摘要以包名与版本为键，而这里每个 workspace 包的版本都是 `0.0.1`，因此一次源码修改不会移动它。`HarnessVariant` 的基线提交加补丁集哈希才是寻址 harness 源码的东西，仅以插件摘要为键的比较会把同一个包的多个代际混在一起。

清单指名的是组件，而不是它们的传递性影响。一个远端工具描述在未重新注册的情况下发生变化的 MCP 服务器，或一个正文引用的文件发生了变化的 skill，都保持原有摘要；只有规范值覆盖到的东西才被寻址。

读取时必需意味着一个不认识 `composition/manifest` 的构建会拒绝含有它的日志。这是有意的取舍——另一种可能是一个构建无声地把被隔离的会话当作干净会话——而它之所以负担得起，只因为根 [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md) 中的预发布立场。

一个每步都变动可见工具集的组合会每步写出一条清单。按 `compositionSha256` 去重使稳定组合恰好只有一条事件，而变动中的组合确实是在为模型可调用范围的真实变化付费，但一个按步开关的作用域限制会用没有消费方加以区分的事件把日志撑大。

Done.

## Commit

`ff87d9953316c6d503188227064cd770a7eaac13` on branch `worktree-agent-aebe381f4ba63be3f` (based on `475de9978`). Three new files: `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-composition-manifest.{md,zh.md,i18n.yaml}` — 118 lines each side, no package code.

## The decisions, in 15 lines

1. `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` = lowercase SHA-256 hex of `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` ``; `componentAddress(id, digest)` = `id@digest`; full 64 hex everywhere stored or compared, truncation is presentation only.
2. Each producer owns its kind's canonical value beside its `ComponentKindMap` declaration merge — the registry and the writer never switch on kind.
3. Canonical values fixed per kind in a table: skill (frontmatter fields + body), prompt-section (name/order/complete + static text, or `null` for a per-assembly provider), tool (the `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` projection), preset (id/trust + include-resolved rows with preset-relative names), plugin (package name + version + `patchLayerSha256`), dynamic-package, agent-provider.
4. `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'` on every descriptor — a provider-evaluated prompt section addresses its registration, not the bytes the model saw; rendered bytes stay in `request/header`.
5. Excluded from every digest: viewing scope, cwd, timestamps, absolute paths, discovery `source`/`rank`, provider name, any per-assembly value.
6. `ComponentRegistry` moves from a flat `Map` to `ScopedLayers` (as `ctx.tools`/`ctx.skills` already are), yielding `list({ kind, scope })` and a derived `layer: 'global' | 'agent'`.
7. `composition/manifest` is a log-only `SessionEventMap` member, **required-on-read** (not `ignorable`) because every consumer keys a refusal on it, and carries **no `@mode`** — `gen-persistence-catalog` rejects the tag on log events; the `@mode`/`@param` rules govern the new Cordis event instead.
8. Payload: `kind`, `version: 1`, `reason`, `presetId?`, `components[] {id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis}`, `compositionSha256`, `dynamicPackagesMounted`, `synthesized[]`. The sketch's `seq` is dropped — the envelope carries it.
9. Writer: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` (`packages/components/components-manifest/`), injecting only `agents` + `components`; on `agent/pre-step` it recomputes and appends only when `compositionSha256` differs — recomputation is what keeps it correct under HMR, late preset mounts, and scope shadowing.
10. Change detection: existing `tools/change`, `system-prompt/change`, `tools/result`, `agent-preset/selected`, `subagent/provider-added|removed` carry the adapters; the one gap is the dynamic Cordis runner, so `dsh-cordis-host-runner` gains `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` (`@mode emit`, unfiltered).
11. A skill is in play once loaded, not once listed: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill`, a `digest` on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource`, never re-parsing the rendered `<skill_content>` block.
12. Quarantine = `dynamicPackagesMounted`, non-empty `synthesized`, **or no manifest at all**; the scorekeeper invariant rejects a `skill` tool result whose digest no preceding manifest names; `dsh-trajectories` gains `includeQuarantined` + a `quarantined` count and refuses those sessions by default.
13. Ledger: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive` (`packages/improvement/archive/`) over `ctx.storage.domain`, tables `variants` (`HarnessVariant`) and `generations` (`id@digest`), statuses `alive`/`dominated`/`promoted`/`deprecated` defined, lineage stored on both ends, mutations mint rows rather than rewrite them.
14. The manifest-versus-ledger invariant lives in `dsh-archive`'s `./invariant`: every `evidenceSessions` entry must carry a manifest occurrence of that exact `id@digest`.
15. Rollout in 7 slices, each green: registry digest+layering → composition-time adapters → manifest writer + event → skill generations → dynamic packages → quarantine consumers → archive ledger.

Acceptance criteria name five fixture directories: `composition-manifest/`, `composition-manifest-mutation/`, `composition-manifest-quarantine/` under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/`, plus keyless unit tests in the scorekeeper and archive packages.

## Open questions I could not settle from the repository

- **Plugin version as a content address.** Every workspace package is `0.0.1`, so a `plugin` digest does not move on a source edit. I recorded it as a Risk and pointed at `HarnessVariant`'s base-commit + patch-set hash; whether the plugin digest should instead incorporate a build-time source hash is unresolved.
- **How `dsh-components-packages` reads the patch layer.** `dsh.profile.bundles` and `cordis.patch.yml` are resolved by the profile composer, which exposes no service; I specified `ctx.loader.entries()` for rows and left the patch-layer read to the slice.
- **Whether the `dynamic-package` source belongs in the canonical value.** `inspectPlugin` returns host/client source; hashing it is precise but couples the digest to a large payload. No consumer exists yet to calibrate against.
- **Where `alive`/`dominated` transitions are written.** The four-goal note assigns them to the experiment plugin, which does not exist; the ledger only owns the record and the transitions here.
- **Whether a subagent's manifest should reference its parent's.** I decided a subagent writes its own manifest into its own session and a deeper scope chain still reads as `layer: 'agent'`; a cross-session lineage field was not settled.

## Gates run

- `pnpm install --offline` — exit 0.
- `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <pair>` — recorded the sidecar.
- `pnpm run doc-sync` — **28 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** in 348s (includes `agent note format`, `agent note classification`, `translation pairing`, `markdown links`, `markdown wrap`, `doc-typecheck`, `doc budgets`, `documentation build`).
- `git diff --cached --check` — clean; the lefthook pre-commit hook (translation pairing, whitespace, vendor guard) passed.

No test/build/lint gates were run: the change is documentation only, adds no package code, and touches no source the type or runtime gates cover.
